TOP.name: addTOP
TOP.description: The Add TOP composites the input images together by adding the pixel values. Output = Input1 + Input2. It clamps a color channel if the sum exceeds 1. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: size
parameters.label: Fixed Layer
parameters.description: ⊞ - The selected input will become the fixed layer and the other input will be the overlay. This does not change the order of the composite (Input1 + Input2), only which layer is considered fixed and which layer is adjustable by the parameters on the Transform page. The resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer is used as the composite's final resolution and aspect ratio unless manually on the Common Page .

parameters.name: prefit
parameters.label: Pre-Fit Overlay
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the Overlay layer (Overlay layer is the input that is NOT the Fixed Layer) fills the composite.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fill the resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: fithorz
parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer horizontally.

parameters.name: fitvert
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer vertically.

parameters.name: fitbest
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretch/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the best possible match that does not crop any of the Overlay layer. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: fitoutside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the worst possible match. This is the opposite of Best Fit. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Overlay is not squashed or stretched. The Overlay layer uses its own resolution and aspect ratio during the composite. Pixel accurate composites require Native Resolution , use this setting for to maintain an image's original resolution during the composite.

parameters.name: justifyh
parameters.label: Justify Horizontal
parameters.description: ⊞ - Specify the horizontal alignment of the Overlay.

parameters.name: left

parameters.name: right

TOP.name: analyzeTOP
TOP.description: The Analyze TOP takes any image and determines various characteristics of it, such as the average pixel color, the pixel with the maximum luminance, or the min and max values in each channel. The result is stored in a 1x1, 1xN or Nx1 image depending on the chosen scope (See Scope parameter below). If the input is a 3D texture, the result is stored in a 1x1x1, 1xNxD, Nx1xD, or 1x1xD image depending on the chosen scope. The calculated values can be brought into CHOPs using the TOP to CHOP node. Note: When using the minimum and maximum operators, the default behaviour is to select the pixel with the highest value as chosen in the Analyze Channel parameter. For example, if Luminance is selected, the output will be the RGBA values of the pixel with the highest luminance, not the luminance value itself. Similarly, if a single channel is selected e.g. Red, Green, Blue, etc, then the output will be the pixel with the highest red value, rather than the highest values in each channel. To find the min or max values in each channel separately, set the Analyze Channel to RGBA Independent. Note: When the operation is set to Count Pixels or Sum, the output image will default to a 32 bit floating point format in order to properly store the output data. For all other operations, the default output format will match the input format. The image format can be set manually using the parameter on the Common page. Note: Using the Exclude NaNs or Mask features will slow down the performance of the node and should only be enabled if they are necessary. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: op
parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: ⊞ - The operation to perform on the input image.

parameters.name: average
parameters.label: Average
parameters.description: Find the average value in each channel of the input image. This operation is notably slower when the Exclude NaNs or Mask features are used as the node must perform two passes to calculate the results.

parameters.name: minimum
parameters.label: Minimum Pixel
parameters.description: Find the pixel with the lowest value as determined by the 'Analyze Channel ' parameter. See Notes in the summary for more details.

parameters.name: maximum
parameters.label: Maximum Pixel
parameters.description: Find the pixel with the highest value as determined by the 'Analyze Channel ' parameter. See Notes in the summary for more details.

parameters.name: count
parameters.label: Count Pixels
parameters.description: Calculates the number of valid pixels in the input image. By default, the output will be fixed based on the dimensions of the image as determined by the ' Scope ' parameter e.g. Full Image = width*height. When Exclude NaNs is enabled or a Mask is defined, the output will be the number of pixels that pass the mask and NaN checks. By default, when counting pixels the output image will be set to a 32bit floating point format.

parameters.name: sum
parameters.label: Sum
parameters.description: Calculates the sum of all pixels in the input image by adding all of the values together. By default, the output image will be set to a 32bit floating point format in order to correctly store the output result.

parameters.name: minrgb
parameters.label: Minimum in RGB
parameters.description: Find the minimum value from the red, green and blue channels. All channels of the output will contain the same minimum value.

parameters.name: minrgba
parameters.label: Minimum in RGBA
parameters.description: Find the minimum value from the red, green, blue and alpha channels. All channels of the output will contain the same minimum value.

parameters.name: maxrgb
parameters.label: Maximum in RGB
parameters.description: Find the maximum value from the red, green and blue channels. All channels of the output will contain the same maximum value.

parameters.name: maxrgba
parameters.label: Maximum in RGBA
parameters.description: Find the maximum value from the red, green, blue and alpha channels. All channels of the output will contain the same maximum value.

parameters.name: analyzechannel
parameters.label: Analyze  Channel
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines what value the operation is being performed on. For example, when the operation is Minimum and the Analyze Channel is Red, the output will be the pixel with the lowest red value (not necessarily the lowest Blue or Green values). To separately find the lowest value in each channel, set this parameter to RGBA Independent.

parameters.name: luminance
parameters.label: Luminance
parameters.description: The output results are based on the luminance of the input pixels. Luminance is the relative intensity of the pixel based on the values in the RGB channels. Note: the output contains the original RGBA values of the pixel with the highest/lowest luminance, not the luminance value itself.

parameters.name: red
parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: Calculations are based only on the value in the red channel.

parameters.name: green
parameters.label: Green
parameters.description: Calculations are based only on the value in the green channel.

parameters.name: blue
parameters.label: Blue
parameters.description: Calculations are based only on the value in the blue channel.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: Calculations are based only on the value in the alpha channel.

parameters.name: rgbaverage
parameters.label: RGB Average
parameters.description: Calculations are based on the average value of the RGB channels.

parameters.name: average
parameters.label: RGBA Average
parameters.description: Calculations are based on the average value of the RGBA channels.

parameters.name: rgbmax
parameters.label: RGB Maximum
parameters.description: Calculations are based on the maximum value of the RGB channels.

parameters.name: max
parameters.label: RGBA Maximum
parameters.description: Calculations are based on the maximum value of the RGBA channels.

parameters.name: independent
parameters.label: RGBA Independent
parameters.description: Calculations are performed on each channels separately. Use this mode if you want to find the highest/lowest values in each channel.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.label: Scope
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how pixels are grouped together to calculate the results.

parameters.name: image
parameters.label: Full Image
parameters.description: Calculations are performed on all pixels of the input image and combined into a single pixel result.

parameters.name: rows
parameters.label: Rows
parameters.description: Calculations are performed on each row of the input separately, resulting in an output image that is one pixel wide and the same number of rows as the input. If the input image is 3D, each slice will be one pixel wide and the same number of rows as the input.

parameters.name: columns
parameters.label: Columns
parameters.description: Calculations are performed on each column of the input separately, resulting in an output image that is one pixel tall and the same number of columns as the input. If the input image is 3D, each slice will be one pixel tall and the same number of columns as the input.

parameters.name: slices
parameters.label: Slices
parameters.description: This scope is for 3D textures only. Calculations are performed on each slice of the input separately, resulting in an output image that is a single pixel for each slice.

parameters.name: excludenans
parameters.label: Exclude NaNs
parameters.description: Enable this parameter to skip pixels with a NaN value in the input image. NaNs typically represent errors in previous calculations (such as dividing by zero), but they can also be used to represent invalid pixels in a point cloud image. When most operations encounter a NaN pixel, the resulting output will always be a NaN, so you must enable this parameter to get valid results. If you do not expect NaN values in your input, it is recommended to leave this parameter turned off since it will reduce performance.

parameters.name: mask
parameters.label: Mask
parameters.description: ⊞ - This parameter allows you to exclude certain pixels based on the values in one or more channels in the input. For example, if set to Alpha, only pixels that have a non-zero value in the alpha will be included. This can be useful, for example, if you need to find the average position of a point cloud image that is using an Active channel to indicate which pixels store valid point data.

parameters.name: none
parameters.label: None
parameters.description: No mask channel. All pixels will be used in the output calculations.

parameters.label: Red
parameters.description: Only pixels with a non-zero value in the red channel will be used.

parameters.name: independent
parameters.label: RGBA Independent
parameters.description: Each channel will act as its own mask, so that only pixels will non-zero values will be used in the output calculations.

TOP.name: antiAliasTOP
TOP.description: The Anti-Alias TOP uses a screen space antialiasing technique called ‘SMAA: Enhanced Subpixel Morphological Antialiasing’. Detailed information here: http://www.iryoku.com/smaa/ It uses an image’s luminance, color or a depth map to detect edges of objects and then applies anti-aliasing to those edges. The current implementation does not yet use the temporal features of it, so each image is individually anti-aliased without requiring knowledge of other frames. It doesn’t require the extra memory that regular Render TOP anti-aliasing does, and avoids work involved with antialiasing polygon edges that are ultimately occluded by another object.

TOP.name: blobTrackTOP
TOP.description: The Blob Track TOP is implemented using OpenCV . To get the results of the Blob Track TOP , attach an Info DAT or Info CHOP to it. The Info reports the current blob IDs, coordinates and sizes in pixels. The blob ID increases for every new blob that is detected. It converts the incoming image to monochrome (since it operates on an single color channel), but to better prepare the image, preceed it with a Monochrome TOP followed by a Luma Level TOP , and adjust Black Level, Brightness and Gamma. Typical usage is connecting a video source (such as Video Device In TOP to the Blob Track TOP ). NOTE: can track an unlimited number of blobs in Pro and Commercial, and up to 2 blobs in the Non-Commercial version of TouchDesigner. See also Blob Track CHOP

parameters.name: reset
parameters.label: Reset
parameters.description: Resets all tracking data and learned background data while this parameter is On.

parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.description: Instantly resets all tracking data and learned background data.

parameters.name: monosource
parameters.label: Mono Source
parameters.description: ⊞ - Blob tracking is done using a single channel. This menu controls what single channel is used to detect blobs.

parameters.name: drawblobs
parameters.label: Draw Blob Bounds
parameters.description: Draws rectangles on the TOP image that shows where the tracked blobs are.

parameters.name: blobcolor
parameters.label: Blob Bound Color
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines the color of the rectangles that are drawn to show the blobs.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.description: Threshold used to create the binary texture when using background subtraction. It is the threshold of the difference between the background texture and the input texture.

parameters.name: downloadtype
parameters.label: Download Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - Gives the option for a delayed data download from the GPU , which is much faster and does not stall the render.

parameters.name: immediate
parameters.label: Immediate (Slow)
parameters.description: Get the current frame's output. Slower.

parameters.name: delayed
parameters.label: Next Frame (Fast)
parameters.description: Get the previous frame's output. Faster.

parameters.name: minblobsize
parameters.label: Minimum Blob Size
parameters.description: Blobs must be at least this big to be tracked.

parameters.name: maxblobsize
parameters.label: Maximum Blob Size
parameters.description: Blobs larger than this will not be tracked.

parameters.name: maxmovedistance
parameters.label: Maximum Move Distance
parameters.description: The maximum distance a blob can move in one frame and still be considered to the same blob (maintain the same ID).

parameters.name: deletenearby
parameters.label: Delete Nearby Blobs
parameters.description: Sometimes (depending on the tracking method) duplicate blobs may be created. This feature allows you to delete blobs that are too close to each other.

parameters.name: deletedist
parameters.label: Minimum Distance
parameters.description: When deleting nearby blobs, blobs will be deleted if they are within this number of pixels of each other. The smaller blob will be deleted.

parameters.name: deletenearbytol
parameters.label: Delete Area Tolerance
parameters.description: Along with the distance, the area of the two blobs can be compared. If this parameter is 1, than the area is ignored. As this parameter gets smaller only blobs that have a significant size difference (between the two blobs being compared) will be deleted.

parameters.name: deleteoverlap
parameters.label: Delete Overlapping Blobs
parameters.description: Deletes blobs that are overlapping.

parameters.name: deleteoverlaptol
parameters.label: Delete Overlap Tolerance
parameters.description: If this parameter is 1 then only blobs that are completely overlapped will be deleted. As this value gets smaller less and less overlap is needed for a blob to get deleted.

parameters.name: reviveblobs
parameters.label: Revive Blobs
parameters.description: When enabled, will revive lost blobs (ie. same ID) if they satisfy all the below parameters

parameters.name: revivetime
parameters.label: Revive Time
parameters.description: The time (in seconds) threshold for reviving a lost blob. If a blob has been lost for longer than revive time, it will not be revived and is considered expired.

parameters.name: revivearea
parameters.label: Revive Area Difference
parameters.description: The area difference threshold for the new blob and the lost blob.

parameters.name: revivedistance
parameters.label: Revive Distance
parameters.description: The distance threshold between the new blob and the lost blob.

parameters.name: includelost
parameters.label: Include Lost Blobs in Table

TOP.name: bloomTOP
TOP.description: The Bloom TOP creates a glow effect around bright parts of the input image that simulates light bouncing around a lens assembly of a camera. Parameters control how much of the bright spots of your input image get bloomed, how wide the bloom gets spread, and how it rolls off into the un-bloomed areas. The bloom starts with a preprocessing stage (Pre-Black Level, Pre-Gamma, and Pre-Brightness), (similar to the Black Level, Brightness, and Gamma parameters of a Level TOP ) which help to isolate the hot spots of the image that the bloom originates from (the Black Level), and boost the hot spots (Gamma and Brightness). (Switch the Output menu for a moment to Pre-Process to make sure you have a good signal to bloom with.) The second stage is a combination of scaled-down (blurred) levels of the pre-processed image: The first level is the original pre-processed image, the second level is scaled down to half size (essentially 4 pixels averaged into one pixel), the third is the second level scaled down to half, and so on until the "top" level is 1x1 pixel (the average of the whole image.) For example, a 1024 x 1024 input images gives 10 levels. (These are called mipmaps.) The second stage blends a range of scaled-down blur levels using the Min Bloom Radius and Max Bloom Radius parameters, where 0 refers to the first scaled-down level and 1 refers to the top scaled-down level. The Min and Max determine how dispersed or smeared the blooming is. Note: If Max<Min, Max is set to Min. In the third stage, the resulting bloom level is increased, reduced and shaped using Bloom Threshold, Bloom S-Curve, Bloom Fill and Bloom Intensity. Typically the Fill and Intensity parameters should be adjusted first, and then some adjustment with Threshold, Min and Max, and with more finesse, the S-Curve if necessary. Tip: If you want to bloom something and composite it over something else or a variant of the original, set the Output parameter to Bloom with Alpha and add it ( Add TOP ) to something else.

parameters.name: preblacklevel
parameters.label: Pre-Black Level
parameters.description: Similar to the Black Level parameter of a Luma Level TOP . Pixels with a luminosity less than this value are pushed to black.

parameters.name: pregamma
parameters.label: Pre-Gamma
parameters.description: Similar to the Gamma parameter of a Luma Level TOP , applies a gamma adjustment to the pixel value after the Pre-Black Level stage, which makes all non-zero values closer to RGB = 1, 1, 1.

parameters.name: prebrightness
parameters.label: Pre-Brightness
parameters.description: Similar to the Brightness parameter of a Luma Level TOP , it is a multiplier for the pixel value after the Pre-Gamma stage.

parameters.name: minbloomradius
parameters.label: Min Bloom Radius
parameters.description: Determines the minimum blur level to start sampling from. It is 0 to 1, so given a 1024x1024 image has 10 blur levels, if Minimum Bloom Size is set to .2, we will begin sampling from blur level 2 (the Pre-process image scaled to one quarter.) (The actual number of blur levels in the image is automatically determined by the image size.)

parameters.name: maxbloomradius
parameters.label: Max Bloom Radius
parameters.description: Determines the maximum blur level we sample from. It is 0 to 1, so if the image has 10 blur levels and a Maximum Bloom Size is set to .8, we will sample mipmap levels up to level 8. If Max<Min, Max is set to Min.

parameters.name: bloomthreshold
parameters.label: Bloom Threshold
parameters.description: After the blur levels have been mixed, this cuts away the darkest part of the image, or, when < 0, it adds more of the full-image average.

parameters.name: bloomscurve
parameters.label: Bloom S-Curve
parameters.description: Reshapes the bloom rolloff so that it is tighter/steeper to the hot spots.

parameters.name: bloomfill
parameters.label: Bloom Fill
parameters.description: Makes the bloom wider.

parameters.name: bloomintensity
parameters.label: Bloom Intensity
parameters.description: Final multiplier of accumulated bloom value.

parameters.name: output
parameters.label: Output
parameters.description: Permits the user to select the image that is output; useful for previewing the outputs of each stage of the bloom pipeline. If set to "Input", the original image is output; if set to "Preprocess", the preprocessed image is output; "Bloom" outputs only the bloom value with alpha = 1; "Bloom with Alpha" outputs only bloom value with its computed alpha (max of R G and B); and "Input + Bloom" (the default) outputs the combined source image and bloom image.

TOP.name: blurTOP
TOP.description: The Blur TOP blurs the image with various kernel filters and radii. It can do multi-pass blurs and can do horizontal, vertical, or z-direction blurs. Use Pre-shrink when the blurs are high and you want to optimize performance. Tip: Filter Size is expressed in pixels. If you want resolution-independent blurs, use an expression like me.par.resolutionw/100 in the Filter Size parameter, which gives a 1% image blur. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: type
parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines the mathematical function used to create the blur.

parameters.name: catmull
parameters.label: Catmull-Rom
parameters.description: A spline approximation to a Gaussian kernel. Gives sharper textures and more accurate edges.

parameters.name: gaussian
parameters.label: Gaussian
parameters.description: A normal distribution where pixels at the center have more effect on the resulting pixel. Gaussian lacks sharpness but handles ringing and aliasing well.

parameters.name: box
parameters.label: Box
parameters.description: Each pixel within the box is weighted evenly. Inexpensive and gives a "boxy" look.

parameters.name: bartlette
parameters.label: Bartlette
parameters.description: A triangle filter. The weight of each pixel is a linear function of its distance from the center.

parameters.name: sinc
parameters.label: Sinc
parameters.description: A sharpening filter. Some pixels contribute a negative weight to the result, artifacts may occur in the form of "ringing". Keeps small details and edges better than Gaussian.

parameters.name: hanning
parameters.label: Hanning
parameters.description: A cosine approximation to a Gaussian kernel.

parameters.name: blackman
parameters.label: Blackman
parameters.description: A higher order cosine approximation to a Gaussian kernel.

parameters.name: extend
parameters.label: Extend
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the extend conditions to determine what happens to the blur at the edge of the image.

parameters.name: hold
parameters.label: Hold
parameters.description: The blur is clamped at the edges.

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.label: Repeat
parameters.description: The blur is calculated as if the image was repeating (tiled - blurring at the bottom of image that would fall outside the image edges will appear at top of image).

parameters.name: mirror
parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.description: The blur is calculated as if the image was mirrored and repeating.

parameters.name: preshrink
parameters.label: Pre-Shrink
parameters.description: Reduces the image's resolution before applying the blur. This effectively applies a 2x2 box filter on the input and creates a smaller texture to do the full blur operation on. It behaves as if the kernel size is made larger, but has less of a performance impact, but also the blur isn't as high quality vs. actually increasing the kernel size. For 3D textures, pre-shrink is applied to the slices only. There is no depth pre-shrinking.

parameters.name: size
parameters.label: Filter Size
parameters.description: The amount of blur in pixels. If you want a resolution-independent blur, use an expression like me.par.resolutionw/100 in this parameter (which would result in a 1% image blur).

parameters.name: scale
parameters.label: Filter Scale
parameters.description: ⊞ - Scales the blur in three different axes. Each component of the Filter Scale is multiplied by the Filter Size to define the total amount of blur for each axis in pixels.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.label: Sample Step
parameters.description: ⊞ - When sampling the image, this determines the distance from each pixel to the sample pixel. When units are set to pixels, it is the number of pixels away from the current pixel which is sampled to blur the image. A Sample Step of 3 would sample pixels 3 pixels away.

parameters.name: offsetunit
parameters.label: Sample Step Unit
parameters.description: Select between Pixel, Fraction, or Fraction Aspect as the units to use for the Sample Step parameter.

parameters.name: rotate
parameters.label: Rotate Kernel
parameters.description: ⊞ - Rotates the blur filter. More noticeable when performing a horizontal blur.

parameters.name: dither
parameters.label: Dither
parameters.description: Enabling makes 8-bit blurs look smoother. This can help if the blur operation introduces banding or other unexpected artifacts.

parameters.name: resmult
parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this TOP is affected by the global multiplier.

(You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

TOP.name: cacheTOP
TOP.description: The Cache TOP stores a sequence of images into GPU memory. These cached images can be read by the graphics card much faster than an image cache in main memory or reading images off disk. The Cache TOP can be used to freeze images in the TOP by turning the Active parameter Off. (You can set the cache size too 1 .) The Cache TOP acts as a delay if you set Output Index to negative numbers and leave the Active parameter On. Once a sequence of images has been captured by turning the Active parameter On or toggling the Active Pulse parameter, they can be looped by animating the Output Index parameter.

parameters.name: active
parameters.label: Active
parameters.description: While this is On, the Cache TOP will capture images into its memory.

parameters.name: activepulse
parameters.label: Active  Pulse
parameters.description: Captures an image for the single frame this was pulsed.

parameters.name: cacheonce
parameters.label: Get One Image on Startup
parameters.description: Checking this On will cook the TOP once after startup to load an initial image.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.label: Replace Single
parameters.description: While this is On, the Cache TOP will replace the image at 'Replace Index' with the input image. This allows you to replace specific images in the cache at will.

parameters.name: replacespulse
parameters.label: Replace  Pulse
parameters.description: Replace an image for the single frame this was pulsed.

parameters.name: replaceindex
parameters.label: Replace Index
parameters.description: Select the image index that will be replaced by the input, when 'Replace Single' is turned on.

parameters.name: prefill
parameters.label: Pre-Fill
parameters.description: Cooks 'Cache Size' number of times to fill the Cache TOP with images. When set to 1, it will fill the cache. If set to 1 during playback, it will fill immediately. If set to 1 and saved out, then next time the file is opened the cache will pre-fill. While this is > 0, the node behaves as if the Active parameter is Off. If set to 0, then back > 0, it will clear the previous data, and pre-fill again. For more information refer to the Pre-Filling article.

parameters.name: prefillpulse
parameters.label: Pre-Fill  Pulse
parameters.description: Pre-fills a single image during the frame this was pulsed.

parameters.name: cachesize
parameters.label: Cache Size
parameters.description: Determines the number of images that can be stored in this Cache TOP .

parameters.name: step
parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.description: The number of cooks that go by before the Cache TOP grabs an image. A Step Size of 2 will cache an image every 2nd cook, a Step Size of 3 will cache every 3rd cook, and so on.

parameters.name: outputindex
parameters.label: Output Index
parameters.description: Determines which image in cache the TOP outputs. 0 is the most recent image, negative integers output image further back in time.

parameters.name: outputindexunit
parameters.label: Output Index Unit
parameters.description: Sets the units used in the Output Index parameter.

parameters.name: interp
parameters.label: Interpolate Frames
parameters.description: When On (On = 1), the Cache TOP will interpolate between frames when non-integer values are used in the Output Index parameter. For example, a value of -0.5 in Output Index will output a blended image of the most recent frame (0.0) and the second most recent frame (-1.0).

parameters.name: alwayscook
parameters.label: Always  Cook
parameters.description: Forces the operator to cook every frame.

parameters.name: reset
parameters.label: Reset
parameters.description: While On this will empty the cache of stored images and release the memory held by the TOP .

parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.label: Reset
parameters.description: Instantly empty the cache.

TOP.name: cHOPtoTOP
TOP.description: The CHOP to TOP puts CHOP channels into a TOP image. By default the texture created will be 32-bit floating point to match the precision of the CHOP data. This can be changed setting the TOP 's Pixel Format to something other than 'Input'. The Data Format parameter determines how the input channels are converted into pixel colors in the output image. For example, when the Data Format is set to 'R', each channel will be interpreted as a row of red pixel data. Likewise, if the Data Format is RGBA, then the first 4 channels will become a set of red, blue, green and alpha data for one row of pixels and each subsequent set of 4 channels will become additional rows. Note: Channels are grouped by their order in the CHOP rather than their names i.e. just because a channel is named g0 or b1 does not mean it will necessarily be be placed in a blue or green pixel. The Image Layout parameter controls how the pixel rows are arranged in the output image. By default, the width of the image will be equal to the number of samples in the CHOP , clamped to a maximum texture width (often 32768) (the sample rate is ignored), and the height will be equal to the number of channel sets. For example, when the Data Format is RGB and the there are 9 input channels (for example, r0 g0 b0 r1 g1 b1 r2 g2 b2), there will be 3 rows of pixels using the default image layout. If the channel length is longer than the image width, the wrapped layout option can be used to continue the channel data onto additional rows of pixels. Each new set of channels will still begin on a new row of pixels. If the Image Layout parameter is set to Fit to Square, the TOP determines the image resolution based on the total number of samples across all channel sets (approximately the square root of the number of samples + 1) in width and height. This layout is most often used for point cloud data, where an efficient layout is preferred and the position of a pixel is not generally important. Unlike in the wrapped layout, channel sets in this mode are appended immediately to the end of the previous set, so that any empty pixels will appear at the end of the image. Where there are some unused pixels, you can fill the unused pixels at the top with a special value based on the Extra Pixel Values parameter, (0, 0, 0, 0) by default. To put (0, 0, 0, -1) you have to set the pixel format to 32-bit float so you can represent negative and positive numbers of any value.

parameters.name: dataformat
parameters.label: Data Format
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the input CHOP channels will be turned into an image. If the CHOP is missing channels required to provide all the data for a scanline, the extra channels are ignored.

parameters.name: r
parameters.label: R
parameters.description: Each channel is treated as the Red channel for a new scanline. Using the default Image Layout , the height of the image will be equal to the number of channels in the CHOP .

parameters.name: rg
parameters.label: RG
parameters.description: The first two channels will be the Red and Green channels for a scanline, the next two channels will be Red and Green for the next scanline, etc. Using the default Image Layout , the height of the image will be half the number of channels in the CHOP , rounded down.

parameters.name: rgb
parameters.label: RGB
parameters.description: The first three channels will be the Red, Green and Blue channels for a scanline, the next three channels will be Red, Green and Blue for the next scanline, etc. Using the default Image Layout , the height of the image will be the number of channels in the CHOP divided by 3, rounded down.

parameters.name: rgba
parameters.label: RGBA
parameters.description: The first four channels will be the Red, Green, Blue, and Alpha channels for a scanline, the next four channels will be Red, Green, Blue and Alpha for the next scanline, etc. Using the default Image Layout , the height of the image will be the number of channels in the CHOP divided by 4, rounded down.

parameters.name: a
parameters.label: A
parameters.description: Each channel is treated as the Alpha channel for a new scanline. Using the default Image Layout , the height of the image will be equal to the number of channels in the CHOP .

parameters.name: legacy
parameters.label: Legacy
parameters.description: This mode only creates a single scanline in all cases. More than 4 channels will not do anything. If the CHOP has 1 or 2 channels, it will set R,G,B,A to the first channel of the CHOP . The 2nd channel is ignored. If it has 3 channels, it sets the 3 channels to R,G,B and A = sample number / # of samples (i.e A is a ramp starting at 0 and climbing to the (width -1). If it has 4 channels, they are set to R,G,B,A.

parameters.name: clamp
parameters.label: Clamp  CHOP  Values
parameters.description: Clamps CHOP values to 0-1 range.

parameters.name: layout
parameters.label: Image  Layout
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls the dimensions of the output image and how the CHOP samples are arranged as pixels. This menu replaces the previous 'Crop Long Channels' and 'Fit to Square' parameters.

parameters.name: rowscropped
parameters.label: Row per Channel Set (Cropped)
parameters.description: Each set of channels, as determined by the Data Format, is converted into a row of pixels in the output image. If the channel length exceeds the maximum texture resolution, or the custom width defined in the Output Resolution , the remaining samples are ignored . This option is equivalent to turning on the previous Crop Long Channels parameter.

parameters.name: rowswrapped
parameters.label: Row(s) per Channel Set (Wrapped)
parameters.description: Each set of channels, as determined by the Data Format, is converted into a row of pixels in the output image. If the channel length exceeds the maximum texture resolution, or the custom width defined in the Output Resolution , the remaining samples will be put into a new row of pixels . Additional channel sets will begin in a new row of the output rather than at the end of the previous set. This option is equivalent to turning off the previous Crop Long Channels parameter.

parameters.name: square
parameters.label: Fit to Square (Combine Sets)
parameters.description: Pixels are arranged in the smallest square texture that fits all of the given CHOP samples. Channel sets, as determined by the Data Format, are wrapped onto the next row of pixels if the CHOP channel length exceeds the width of the texture. Unlike the wrapped layout, the next channel set will begin at the next available pixel rather than starting in a new row. This option is equivalent to turning off the old 'Crop Long Channels' parameter and turning on the previous 'Fit to Square' parameter. This layout is most often used for point cloud data, where the position of a pixel in the image is not generally important.

parameters.name: rgba
parameters.label: Extra Pixel Values (RGBA)
parameters.description: ⊞ - If the current Image Layout results in more pixels than there are available samples in the input CHOP , the values specified here will be used to fill in the extra pixels. (All textures require full rows of pixels, in other words all rows of pixels have the same number of pixels.)

TOP.name: chromaKeyTOP
TOP.description: The Chroma Key TOP pulls a key matte from the image using Hue, Saturation, and Value settings. If a pixel falls between the Min and Max parameters for all three settings, then it is included in the key. It outputs an alpha map, or the image with the key color removed. See also the chromaKey component in the Palette , which is a user interface around the Chroma Key TOP that lets you grab frames on-the-fly and interactively set the key color ranges. The UI also adds edge softening and color spill controls. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

TOP.name: circleTOP
TOP.description: The Circle TOP can be used to generate circles, ellipses and N-sided polygons. The shapes can be customized with different sizes, rotation and positioning. An optional border can be added to the shape. Background, border and fill colors can all be set independently. Anti-aliasing can be turned on or off. You can use the arc angles to cut out part of the shape. In the case of polygons, the number of visible sides will be preserved no matter how much is cut out.

parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.name: width
parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.name: height
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.name: best
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.name: outside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.description: ⊞ - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.name: nearest
parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: linear
parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get TOP images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.description: Uses mipmap filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.name: npasses
parameters.label: Passes
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the TOP the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the GLSL TOP when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected TOP 's image.

parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the TOP will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.name: format
parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.description: ⊞ - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to Pixel Formats for more information.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does not apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to sRGB .

parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working Color Space before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: srgb
parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.description: Rec.601 with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec709
parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.description: Rec.709 color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020 color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.description: DCI-P3 color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim" color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.description: 1 - ACES 2065-1 (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acescg
parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.name: useparent
parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.description: Will use the Reference White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use Parent ' selected, then 'UI Reference White' will be used.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: ui
parameters.label: UI
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI Reference White Nits' value for it's brightness.

parameters.description: Total amount of texture memory used by this TOP .

inputs.description: Composite Input - Control the Composite operation via the parameters on the Output Page of this operator.

TOP.name: compositeTOP
TOP.description: The Composite TOP is a multi-input TOP that will perform a composite operation for each input. Select the composite operation using the Operation parameter on the Composite parameter page. Note: See also the blendModes component in the Palette . Refer also to OP Snippets . Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: top
parameters.label: TOP
parameters.description: In addition to all the inputs attached, you can specify more using the TOPs listed in this field. Example: ramp* will composite all TOPs whose name starts with ramp .

parameters.name: previewgrid
parameters.label: Preview Grid
parameters.description: This outputs an image showing the effect of all operation types in a grid, with the inputs swapped on the right side of each tile.

parameters.name: selectinput
parameters.label: Select Input
parameters.description: Instead of doing the composites, this causes only one of the inputs to pass through.

parameters.name: inputindex
parameters.label: Input Index
parameters.description: When passing through an input with Select Input on, this is the index of the image that is passed through.

parameters.name: operand
parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: ⊞ - Choose which composite operation is performed from this menu. Search the web for 'blend modes' for more detailed information on the effects of each type.

parameters.name: add
parameters.label: Add
parameters.description: input1.rgba + input2.rgba

parameters.name: atop
parameters.label: Atop
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * input2.a) + (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a))

parameters.name: average
parameters.label: Average
parameters.description: (input1.rgba + input2.rgba)/2

parameters.name: difference
parameters.label: Difference
parameters.description: absoluteValue(input1.rgb - input2.rgb). Alpha always equals 1.0

parameters.name: divide
parameters.label: Divide
parameters.description: input1.rgba / input2.rgba

parameters.name: inside
parameters.label: Inside
parameters.description: input1.rgba * clamp(input2.a, 0.0, 1.0)

parameters.name: maximum
parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.description: max(input1.r, input2.r), max(input1.g, input2.g), max(input1.b, input2.b), max(input1.a, input2.a)

parameters.name: minimum
parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.description: min(input1.r, input2.r), min(input1.g, input2.g), min(input1.b, input2.b), min(input1.a, input2.a)

parameters.name: outside
parameters.label: Outside
parameters.description: input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)

parameters.name: over
parameters.label: Over
parameters.description: (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a)) + input1.rgba

parameters.name: screen
parameters.label: Screen
parameters.description: 1.0 - ((1.0 - input1.rgba) * (1.0 - input2.rgba))

parameters.name: subtract
parameters.label: Subtract
parameters.description: input1.rgba - input2.rgba

parameters.name: under
parameters.label: Under
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)) + input2.rgba

parameters.name: xor
parameters.label: Xor
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)) + (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a))

parameters.name: swaporder
parameters.label: Swap Operation Order
parameters.description: Swaps the order of the input pairs. A operation B is changed to B operation A. Operations like Add don't matter, but many do, like Over and Hard Light.

parameters.name: size
parameters.label: Fixed Layer
parameters.description: ⊞ - The selected input will become the fixed layer and the other input will be the overlay. This does not change the order of the composite (Input1 + Input2), only which layer is considered fixed and which layer is adjustable by the parameters on the Transform page. The resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer is used as the composite's final resolution and aspect ratio unless manually on the Common Page

parameters.name: prefit
parameters.label: Pre-Fit Overlay
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the Overlay layer (Overlay layer is the input that is NOT the Fixed Layer) fills the composite.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fill the resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: fithorz
parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer horizontally.

parameters.name: fitvert
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer vertically.

parameters.name: fitbest
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretch/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the best possible match that does not crop any of the Overlay layer. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: fitoutside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the worst possible match. This is the opposite of Best Fit. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Overlay is not squashed or stretched. The Overlay layer uses its own resolution and aspect ratio during the composite. Pixel accurate composites require Native Resolution , use this setting for to maintain an image's original resolution during the composite.

parameters.name: justifyh
parameters.label: Justify Horizontal
parameters.description: ⊞ - Specify the horizontal alignment of the Overlay.

parameters.name: left
parameters.label: Left
parameters.description: The Overlay is aligned to the left side of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: center
parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The Overlay is centered in the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: right
parameters.label: Right
parameters.description: The Overlay is aligned to the right side of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: justifyv
parameters.label: Justify Vertical
parameters.description: ⊞ - Specify the vertical alignment of the Overlay.

parameters.name: bottom
parameters.label: Bottom
parameters.description: The Overlay is aligned to the bottom of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: center
parameters.label: Center
parameters.description: The Overlay is centered in the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: top
parameters.label: Top
parameters.description: The Overlay is aligned to the top of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: extend
parameters.label: Extend Overlay
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the extend (or repeat) conditions of the Overlay layer. This parameter determines what happens at the edges of the Overlay layer.

parameters.name: hold
parameters.label: Hold
parameters.description: The pixel values at the edges of the Overlay layer continue to extend past that edge.

parameters.name: zero
parameters.label: Zero
parameters.description: The image does not extend past the edges of the Overlay.

parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . TOP.name: convolveTOP
TOP.description: The Convolve TOP uses a DAT table containing numeric coefficients. For each pixel, it combines its RGBA values and it's neighboring pixels' RGBA values by multiplying the values by the corresponding coefficients in the table, adding the results together. For example, if the table is 5 rows and 5 columns, the pixel and its 24 neighbors are combined. Example coefficient for 3x3 blur, edge, emboss, sharpen and vertical slope kernels. Be sure to turn on 'Normalize Coefficients' to use these coefficients as -is: Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: dat
parameters.label: Coefficients  DAT
parameters.description: The DAT containing the rows and columns of coefficients.

parameters.name: normalize
parameters.label: Normalize Coefficients
parameters.description: This will normalize the coefficients before using them in the convolve. Normaliziation is done by summing all the coefficients and dividing every coefficient by that sum. Note: If the coefficients add up to 0, then this parameter does nothing.

parameters.name: applytoalpha
parameters.label: Apply to Alpha
parameters.description: When off, the alpha channel will not be convolved.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.label: Offset
parameters.description: After the convolution, this value will be added to the R, G and B of the pixel (and A if enabled).

parameters.name: scale
parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: After the convolution, this value will be multiplied to the sum of the RGB(A) of the pixel and the offset.

parameters.name: convolvez
parameters.label: Convolve Z
parameters.description: When on, the DAT table will be defined as a 3D kernel. The size of the 3D kernel must be cubic where the width, height, and depth are equal in size. For example, for a 5x5x5 kernel, there must be 25 rows and 5 columns. The first 5 rows define the coefficients for the first slice of the 3D convolution in a 3D texture. The next 5 rows define the 2nd slice and so on.

For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

TOP.name: cubeMapTOP
TOP.description: The Cube Map TOP builds a texture map in the Cube Map internal texture format. It accepts a vertical cross image, or 1 input per side of the cube. The Phong MAT can use the cube maps from the Cube Map TOP for reflections. The Render TOP can also create cube maps. You can sample a cube map in a GLSL shader by declaring them like this uniform samplerCube < name > ; and sampling them using this in GLSL 3.30+ texture ( samplerCube name , vec3 texcoords ) or this in GLSL 1.20 textureCube ( samplerCube name , vec3 texcoords )

TOP.name: depthTOP
TOP.description: The Depth TOP reads an image containing depth information from a scene described in a specified Render TOP . The resulting image is black (0) at pixels where the surface is at the near depth value (Camera's parameter "Near"). It is white (1) at pixels where the surface is at the far depth value (parameter "Far"). The Depth TOP is used to do shadow mapping. It can have many other uses also, such as edge detection based on depth. The depth range is by definition the near plane -> far plane. Values in the Depth TOP will be 0 at the near plane, and 1 at the far plane. Generally the image in the Depth TOP will be white, unless you have your planes really tight around your object. But just because you can't visually see anything, it doesn't mean the information isn't there. Another option is Linear Camera-Space Depth. If the Render TOP 's Depth Buffer Format is set to 32-Bit Floating-Point and its Linear Camera-Space Depth parameter is on, then the Depth TOP will output linear camera space depth. You can use the Level TOP to re-range the Depth TOP 's values. However make sure you set the Pixel Format of the Level TOP to 16 or 32-bit, or you'll lose a lot of information from the Depth TOP 's data (The Depth TOP has 24-bit data). The Depth TOP creates a 24-bit fixed-point or 32-bit floating-point single channel image. When the Depth TOP is used as an input to another TOP , its data will be treated like an RGBA value of (D, D, D, 1). The same is true when sampling a depth texture in a GLSL shader.

TOP.name: directDisplayOutTOP
TOP.description: NOTE License: Only available in TouchDesigner Educational , TouchDesigner Commercial and TouchDesigner Pro . The Direct Display Out TOP uses new technology available in Vulkan which allows directly outputting the DisplayPort/HDMI ports on the GPU , without interacting with the Windows Desktop. This avoids the need for a Window COMP , avoids cases where other windows and the mouse cursor will go in front of the content window, and avoids a lot of the issues caused by the Windows Compositor, as described Perfect Playback . Up to 3 outputs can be controlled via Direct Display. Requirements: A TouchDesigner Educational, Commercial or Pro license. Workstation Nvidia GPU (Nvidia RTX/Quadro). Geforce will not be able to remove displays from the desktop using configureDdisplay.exe. Windows 11 Pro For Workstations or Windows 11 Enterprise version. Needed to remove the output from the desktop. Once the above requirements are met, the next step is to setup the outputs. If using indiviual outputs, you can setup the resolution/refresh rate in the Nvidia Control Panel . To sync up multiple outputs on a single machine, use the configureMosaic.exe tool from Nvidia or the Nvidia Control Panel first to setup your Mosaic configuration. Make sure the resolution/refresh rate of the display is what is desired. Next remove the display(s) from the desktop so they can be directly controlled by Direct Display. This must be done using configureDdisplay.exe tool from Nvidia . For example you can list the monitors using configureDdisplay status and then remove monitor index 1 using configureDdisplay remove-from-desktop -i 1 If you want to use Quadro Sync/Hardware Frame Lock, use the QSync Utility to configure that now. Quadro Sync Hardware Frame Lock is supported in Pro versions, allowing multiple GPUs to output in sync across multiple TouchDesigner instances. Once this is all done, the Direct Display Out TOP will be able to find and output to the outputs. Some additional information can be found in this talk starting at 32:42. Or on page 72 in the .pdf attached to the talk.

TOP.name: displaceTOP
TOP.description: The Displace TOP will cause one image to be warped by another image. A pixel of the output image at (Uo,Vo, Wo) gets its RGBA value from a different pixel (Ui, Vi, Wi) of the Source Image by using the second input image (the Displace Image). For each pixel in the output image, three factors affect which pixel to fetch from the source: The horizontal, vertical, and z source channels of the Displace Image (Red, Green, and Blue by default). the Uo, Vo, Wo coordinate of the output pixel. A constant Ua, Va, Wa anchor point (Offset). Displace Image - In using the Displace Image, for each pixel in the output, it gets the corresponding pixel from the input, and uses the red channel, green channel, and blue channel as its U, V, and W displacement. If the red, green, and blue are .5, .5, .5, then Uo = Ui, Vo = Vi, Wo = Wi. That is, there is no warp if the Displace Image is a 50% grey. Also the warp is reduced to 0 if the Displace Weight is 0. Where red < .5 in the Displace Image, it fetches a pixel from the left of Uo in the Source Image. If green < .5, it fetches a pixel from below Vo in the Source Image. If blue < .5, it fetches a pixel from slices in front of Wo in the Source Image where w = 0 is the frontmost slice. Thus the pixel is retrieved from Ui, Vi, Wi at Uo*Scale*(red-.5), Vo*Scale*(.5-green), Wo*Scale*(.5-blue) of the Source Image. Uo, Vo, Wo offset - By default, the warping of each output pixel is relative to its Uo, Vo, Wo. But when the UV Weight parameter is 0, the displacement is relative to the center pixel of the Source Image. Ua, Va, Wa anchor (offset) point - This zooms into a pixel of the input if you bring the two other weights down to 0. For the Displace Image, you can change which of its RGBA channels cause the warp. You can choose if there is wraparound in the image warping. If the computed Uo, Vo, Wo is less than 0 or greater than 1, it can wraparound, clamp or mirror. The Displace Image can be any photograph followed by a Slope TOP , which will give luminance gradients in red and green, with the neutral value at .5, exactly the form required by the Displace TOP . One way to experiment is to make a Displace Image from Ramp TOPs. Alternately use a Constant TOP set to .5, .5, .5, 1, then subtract a photo using a Subtract TOP , and add another photo image using an Add TOP . Before subtracting and adding the images, you can lower their effect using Level TOPs and adjusting Brightness. See also: Remap TOP , Lookup TOP Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

TOP.name: edgeTOP
TOP.description: The Edge TOP finds edges in an image and highlights them. For each pixel, it looks at the values at neighboring pixels, and where differences are greater than a threshold, the output's value is higher. See also the Convolve TOP . Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

TOP.name: feedbackTOP
TOP.description: The Feedback TOP can be used to create feedback effects in TOPs. It can give fake motion blur by not clearing the color buffer. The Feedback TOP 's input image will be passed through whenever Feedback is bypassed (by setting the Bypass Feedback parameter = 1). When feedback is activated ( Bypass Feedback parameter = 0) the Feedback TOP will output an image stream sourced from its Target TOP . By selecting a Target TOP downstream in the feedback network, other filter TOPs can be added in between the Feedback TOP and its Target TOP to achive feedback effects. See the example networks below. See OP Snippets for some examples on how to use the Feedback TOP . Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space

parameters.name: useparent
parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel

parameters.name: frontupright
parameters.label: Front Up Right

TOP.name: functionTOP
TOP.description: The Function TOP can perform mathematical operations like sin, cos, or exp on the color values of the input image. Different functions can be performed on each color channel. Some functions will take an additional value from the Base, Exponent or Constant Value parameters, and some functions take an additional input value from the second input image. For some functions, you can use the 'Replace Errors' parameter to insert a new value for values that would otherwise be undefined e.g. log(-1) Supported functions: Input - Pass along the input value unchanged Constant - Replace the input with the value of the 'Constant' parameter. Square Root - Find the square root of the input value i.e. sqrt(x). Absolute Value - Get the absolute value of the input i.e. abs(x). Sign - Returns -1 if the input value is below 0, 0 if it equals 0, and 1 if it's greater than zero. Cosine - Returns the cosine of the input. 1 Sine - Returns the sine of the input. 1 Tangent - Returns the tangent of the input. 1 Arccosine - Returns the arccosine of the input i.e. acos(x). 1 Arcsine - Returns the sine of the input i.e. asin(x). 1 Arctan (Input1) - Returns the arctangent of the input i.e. atan(x). 1 Arctan (Input1 / Input2) - Returns the arctangent of input1 over input2 i.e. atan(x,y). 1 Hyperbolic Cosine - Returns the hyperbolic cosine of the input i.e. cosh(x). 1 Hyperbolic Sine - Returns the sine of the input i.e. sinh(x). 1 Hyperbolic Tangent - Returns the tangent of the input i.e. tanh(x). 1 Log Base 10 - Returns the base 10 logarithm of the input i.e. log10(x). Log Base 2 - Returns the base 2 logarithm of the input i.e. log2(x). Log Base N - Returns the base N logarithm of the input, where N is set by the 'Base Value' parameter. Natural Log - Returns the natural log of the input i.e. ln(x). Exponent - Returns e to the power of the input i.e. e^x. Exponent 2 - Returns 2 to the power of the input i.e. 2^x. Exponent 10 - Returns 10 to the power of the input i.e. 10^x. Base Power - Returns the 'Base Value' parameter to the power of x. 2 Input1 ^ Exponent - Returns the input value to the power of the exponent parameter. 2 Input1 ^ Input2 - Returns the value of input 1 to the power of input 2. 2 dB to Power - Converts decibels to power.

TOP.name: gLSLMultiTOP
TOP.description: The GLSL Multi TOP renders a GLSL shader into a TOP image. Its parameters and functionality are identical to the GLSL TOP , except it allows for more than 3 inputs. Refer to the GLSL TOP help page for more information.

parameters.label: GLSL Version
parameters.description: ⊞ - Pick what version of GLSL to compile the shader with.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - Choose what type of shader you are writing, vertex/pixel shader, or a compute shader.

parameters.label: Vertex   Shader

parameters.name: pixeldat
parameters.label: Pixel  Shader
parameters.description: Points to the DAT holding the Pixel Shader . Drag & Drop a DAT here, or manually enter the path to the DAT .

parameters.description: When this button is pressed the node will try to pre-fill all it's uniform parameter with uniforms that are declare in the shader. Note that the shader compiler will likely not expose uniforms that are unused.

parameters.label: Auto Dispatch Size
parameters.description: Automatically set the dispatch size based on the compute shader's local size and the output texture resolution. Ensures at least one thread per pixel will execute.

parameters.name: dispatchsize

parameters.description: ⊞ - The dispatch size to use when executing a compute shader.

parameters.name: outputaccess

parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how the output textures will be accessed. If the textures will be read from (such as using previous frame's values), then the access should be changed to Read-Write instead of Write Only.

parameters.label: Read
parameters.description: Write readwrite -

parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - Specify what type of texture to create. When creating a 3D texture the TOP will render once for every slice of the output. Refer to 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays for more info.

parameters.name: texture2d
parameters.label: 2D Texture
parameters.description: Creates a 2D texture.

parameters.name: texture2darray
parameters.label: 2D Texture Array
parameters.description: Creates a 2D Texture Array . Slices of the array can be access using a non-normalized integer index for the w coordinate.

parameters.name: texture3d
parameters.label: 3D Texture
parameters.description: Creates a 3D Texture . Slices of the array can be accessed using the w coordinate in the range 0-1. Value of the texture in between slices are interpolated.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.label: Depth
parameters.description: ⊞ - Set the depth of the 3D texture from the Input or the Custom Depth parameter.

parameters.name: customdepth
parameters.label: Custom Depth
parameters.description: Manually set the depth of the 3D texture, otherwise it will use the depth of the input.

parameters.name: inputmapping
parameters.label: Input Mapping
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the node's input(s) are passed into the shader for use when creating a 3D Texture. By default all of the inputs are passed to each slice. When using the N inputs per Slice mode, the first N inputs are passed to the first slice, the next N inputs are passed the second slice, and so on. When it runs out of inputs it loops back to the first input. N is selected by the parameter N Value .

parameters.name: nval
parameters.label: N Value
parameters.description: Determines how many inputs are passed to the shader per slice when using the N inputs per Slice mode for Input Mapping . If for example this is set to 2, then the first 2 inputs will be passed to the first slice, the next 2 inputs will be passed the second slice, and so on. It will loop back to the start of the inputs if it runs out before it reaches the last slice.

parameters.name: inputextenduv
parameters.label: Input Extend Mode UV
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls what is returned from your texture sampling functions when the U and V texture coordinates (called S and T in the shader) are outside [0-1] range.

parameters.name: inputextendw
parameters.label: Input Extend Mode W
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls what is returned from your texture sampling functions when the W texture coordinate (called W in the shader) are outside [0-1] range. Only useful for 3D Texture .

parameters.label: CHOP  Uniforms allow you to send  CHOP  channel data into a GLSL shader as an array. Depending on the array type used, the number of values you can send into the shader may be limited. If you are using Uniform Arrays, you can use the Built
parameters.description: In variable int(var('SYS_GFX_GLSL_MAX_UNIFORMS')) to get an idea of how many values you can pass to the shader. Current GPUs are vec4 based for uniform arrays, so the maximum array size is int(var('SYS_GFX_GLSL_MAX_UNIFORMS')) / 4 . Other uniforms will take away from this maximum. If you are using Texture Buffers the maximum array size is far bigger, int(var('SYS_GFX_MAX_TEXTURE_BUFFER_SIZE')) will tell you the max for this. The max for texture buffer is per texture buffer, and having multiple texture buffers does not take away from the max for each array.

For a CHOP with a single channel declare your uniform as a float, for one with two channels declare your uniform as a vec2, etc. The data is interleaved in the uniform. I.e the .x component is the 1st channel, .y is the 2nd channel, etc.
