parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 2x
parameters.label: 2X
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 4x
parameters.label: 4X
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 8x
parameters.label: 8X
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: fit
parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.description: Fits the width and height to the resolution given below, while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.description: The width and height are limited to the resolution given below. If one of the dimensions exceeds the given resolution, the width and height will be reduced to fit inside the given limits while maintaining the aspect ratio.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.description: Enables the Resolution parameter below, giving direct control over width and height.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: ⊞ - Enabled only when the Resolution parameter is set to Custom Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.name: resmult
parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this TOP is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.name: aspect
parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.description: ⊞ - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.name: armenu
parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.description: ⊞ - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the TOP .

parameters.name: nearest
parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: linear
parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get TOP images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.description: Uses mipmap filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determine how the TOP image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.name: width
parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.name: height
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.name: best
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.name: outside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.description: ⊞ - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.name: nearest
parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: linear
parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get TOP images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.description: Uses mipmap filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.name: npasses
parameters.label: Passes
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the TOP the specified number of times. Making this larger than 1 is essentially the same as taking the output from each pass, and passing it into the first input of the node and repeating the process. Other inputs and parameters remain the same for each pass.

parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the TOP will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.name: format
parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.description: ⊞ - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to Pixel Formats for more information.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace.

parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working Color Space before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: srgb
parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.description: Rec.601 with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec709
parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.description: Rec.709 color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020 color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.description: DCI-P3 color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim" color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.description: 1 - ACES 2065-1 (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acescg
parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.name: useparent
parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.description: Will use the Reference White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use Parent ' selected, then 'UI Reference White' will be used.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: ui
parameters.label: UI
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI Reference White Nits' value for it's brightness.

parameters.description: Horizontal resolution of the TOP in pixels.

parameters.label: resy

parameters.description: Depth of 2D or 3D array if this TOP contains a 2D or 3D texture array.

parameters.label: gpu_memory_used
parameters.description: Total amount of texture memory used by this TOP .

parameters.label: cook_frame

parameters.label: errors

A shader is programmed in Text DATs and referenced by a GLSL Material or a GLSL TOP . Shaders are composed of up to three parts: Vertex Shader, Pixel Shader and Compute Shader.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python Script or GLSL Shader, but can be any multi-line text. Tables are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: The width and height of an image in pixels. Most TOPs, like the  Movie File In TOP  can set the image resolution. See  Aspect Ratio  for the width/height ratio of an image, taking into account non
parameters.description: square pixels.

TOP.name: gLSLTOP
TOP.description: The GLSL TOP renders a GLSL shader into a TOP image. Use the Info DAT to check for compile errors in your shaders. The GLSL TOP can act as a pixel shader, or the more general and complex Compute Shader . Caveat: Compute Shaders need GLSL 4.30 or later. The GLSL TOP has one docked compute shader as well as a normal GLSL shader. Change he Mode to Compute Shader . it will use the glsl1_compute DAT . Refer to the Write a GLSL TOP article for more info on using this TOP . See the GLSL Category for more information, and Compute Shader .

parameters.name: glslversion
parameters.label: GLSL Version
parameters.description: ⊞ - Pick what version of GLSL to compile the shader with.

parameters.name: mode
parameters.label: Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - Choose what type of shader you are writing, vertex/pixel shader, or a compute shader.

parameters.name: predat
parameters.label: Preprocess Directives
parameters.description: Use this DAT to place preprocessor directives at the start of your shader, such as #extension. This is required since these need to be the first lines in the shader, and TouchDesigner will be adding code to the start of your shader to declare uniforms/functions which would appear before #extension directives located in the main shader. #include statements should be avoided unless include-guards are in the DATs. This should not be used for pre-prending common code to your shaders. Use #include statements in the main shader to do that.

parameters.name: vertexdat
parameters.label: Vertex   Shader
parameters.description: Points to the DAT holding the Vertex Shader . Drag & Drop a DAT here, or manually enter the path to the DAT .

parameters.name: pixeldat
parameters.label: Pixel  Shader
parameters.description: Points to the DAT holding the Pixel Shader . Drag & Drop a DAT here, or manually enter the path to the DAT .

parameters.name: computedat
parameters.label: Compute  Shader
parameters.description: Points to the DAT holding the Compute Shader . Drag & Drop a DAT here, or manually enter the path to the DAT .

parameters.name: loaduniformnames
parameters.label: Load Uniform Names
parameters.description: When this button is pressed the node will try to pre-fill all it's uniform parameter with uniforms that are declare in the shader. Note that the shader compiler will likely not expose uniforms that are unused.

parameters.name: dispatchsize
parameters.label: Dispatch Size
parameters.description: ⊞ - The dispatch size to use when executing a compute shader.

parameters.name: outputaccess
parameters.label: Output Access
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how the output textures will be accessed. If the textures will be read from (such as using previous frame's values), then the access should be changed to Read-Write instead of Write Only.

parameters.name: writeonly
parameters.label: Write Only
parameters.description: The texture will only be written to by the shader, not read.

parameters.name: readwrite
parameters.label: Read-Write
parameters.description: The texture will be both written and read by the shader.

parameters.name: type
parameters.label: Output Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - Specify what type of texture to create. When creating a 3D texture the TOP will render once for every slice of the output. Refer to 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays for more info.

parameters.name: texture2d
parameters.label: 2D Texture
parameters.description: Creates a 2D texture.

parameters.name: texture2darray
parameters.label: 2D Texture Array
parameters.description: Creates a 2D Texture Array . Slices of the array can be access using a non-normalized integer index for the w coordinate.

parameters.name: texture3d
parameters.label: 3D Texture
parameters.description: Creates a 3D Texture . Slices of the array can be accessed using the w coordinate in the range 0-1. Value of the texture in between slices are interpolated.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.label: Depth
parameters.description: ⊞ - Set the depth of the 3D texture from the Input or the Custom Depth parameter.

parameters.name: customdepth
parameters.label: Custom Depth
parameters.description: Manually set the depth of the 3D texture, otherwise it will use the depth of the input.

parameters.name: autodispatchsize
parameters.label: Auto Dispatch Size
parameters.description: Automatically set the dispatch size based on the compute shader's local size and the output texture resolution. Ensures at least one thread per pixel will execute.

parameters.name: clearoutputs
parameters.label: Clear Outputs
parameters.description: When using a Compute Shader , this controls if the output texture should be cleared at the start of each cook. Otherwise the data from the previous cook will stay in the texture, and pixels can be left as-is in the Compute Shader .

parameters.name: clearvalue
parameters.label: Clear Value
parameters.description: ⊞ - The color value to clear all pixels to at the start of the cook.

parameters.name: inputmapping
parameters.label: Input Mapping
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the node's input(s) are passed into the shader for use when creating a 3D Texture. By default all of the inputs are passed to each slice. When using the N inputs per Slice mode, the first N inputs are passed to the first slice, the next N inputs are passed the second slice, and so on. When it runs out of inputs it loops back to the first input. N is selected by the parameter N Value .

parameters.name: nval
parameters.label: N Value
parameters.description: Determines how many inputs are passed to the shader per slice when using the N inputs per Slice mode for Input Mapping . If for example this is set to 2, then the first 2 inputs will be passed to the first slice, the next 2 inputs will be passed the second slice, and so on. It will loop back to the start of the inputs if it runs out before it reaches the last slice.

parameters.name: inputextenduv
parameters.label: Input Extend Mode UV
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls what is returned from your texture sampling functions when the U and V texture coordinates (called S and T in the shader) are outside [0-1] range.

parameters.name: inputextendw
parameters.label: Input Extend Mode W
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls what is returned from your texture sampling functions when the W texture coordinate (called W in the shader) are outside [0-1] range. Only useful for 3D Texture .

parameters.name: numcolorbufs
parameters.label: # of Color Buffers
parameters.description: Any shader you write can output to more than one RGBA buffer at a time. Turn up this value to have more color buffers allocated for you, and refer to [Write_a_GLSL_ TOP #Outputting_to_Multiple_Color_Buffers Write a GLSL TOP ] for more information on using this feature.

parameters.name: simplexnoise
parameters.label: TDSimplexNoise()
parameters.description: ⊞ - Pick between Performance vs Quality Simplex noise. Performance mode picks the existing TDSimplexNoise(). Quality noise reduces certain artifacts and axis alignment issues with the existing simplex noise at the cost of speed.

parameters.name: performance
parameters.label: Performance
parameters.description: Performant noise.

parameters.name: quality
parameters.label: Quality
parameters.description: Quality noise.

parameters.name: premultrgbbyalpha
parameters.label: Pre-Multiply RGB by Alpha
parameters.description: Multiplies the RGB values in all the Color parameters by their Alpha value, before passing them to the shader.

parameters.name: color0name
parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the uniform in the shader to assign this color value to.

parameters.name: color0rgb
parameters.label: RGB
parameters.description: ⊞ - The RGB values for this uniform.

parameters.name: color0alpha
parameters.label: Alpha
parameters.description: The Alpha value for this uniform.

parameters.name: vec
parameters.label: Vector
parameters.description: Sequence of vector uniforms

parameters.name: vec0name
parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The uniform name, as declared in the shader

parameters.name: vec0value
parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: ⊞ - The value(s) to give the uniform.

parameters.label: CHOP  Uniforms allow you to send  CHOP  channel data into a GLSL shader as an array. Depending on the array type used, the number of values you can send into the shader may be limited. If you are using Uniform Arrays, you can use the Built
parameters.description: In variable int(var('SYS_GFX_GLSL_MAX_UNIFORMS')) to get an idea of how many values you can pass to the shader. Current GPUs are vec4 based for uniform arrays, so the maximum array size is int(var('SYS_GFX_GLSL_MAX_UNIFORMS')) / 4 . Other uniforms will take away from this maximum. If you are using Texture Buffers the maximum array size is far bigger, int(var('SYS_GFX_MAX_TEXTURE_BUFFER_SIZE')) will tell you the max for this. The max for texture buffer is per texture buffer, and having multiple texture buffers does not take away from the max for each array.

parameters.name: array
parameters.label: Array
parameters.description: Sequence of array uniforms

parameters.name: array0name
parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the uniform. You can send up to 4 channels into the GLSL shader in a single uniform. The number of channels is determined by the float/vec2/vec3/vec4 menu to the right of the name. For a CHOP with a single channel declare your uniform as a float, for one with two channels declare your uniform as a vec2, etc. The data is interleaved in the uniform. I.e the .x component is the 1st channel, .y is the 2nd channel, etc.

parameters.name: array0type
parameters.label: Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - The data type of the uniform in the shader.

parameters.name: array0chop
parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.description: The channels from this CHOP will be sent to the GLSL shader.

parameters.name: array0arraytype
parameters.label: Array Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - The type of the uniform.

parameters.name: uniformarray
parameters.label: Uniform Array
parameters.description: All GPUs can send array data into a GLSL shader using Uniform Arrays.

parameters.name: texturebuffer
parameters.label: Texture Buffer
parameters.description: Newer GPUs can send array data into a GLSL shader using Texture Buffers. Texture Buffers use texture memory and texture fetches to access the data, which allows them to store many more values.

parameters.label: Where i is the 0
parameters.description: based index (an integer) into the buffer that you want to get a value for.

parameters.name: matrix
parameters.label: Matrix
parameters.description: Sequence of matrix uniforms

parameters.name: matrix0name
parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the matrix uniform.

parameters.name: matrix0value
parameters.label: Matrix
parameters.description: The value to assign the matrix. For valid ways to specify this, see the Matrix Parameters article.

parameters.name: ac
parameters.label: Atomic Counter
parameters.description: Sequence of atomic counter uniforms

parameters.name: ac0name
parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The name of the uniform.

parameters.name: ac0initvalue
parameters.label: Initial Value Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - Specifies how the atomic counters receive their initial value, either through a single default value or a CHOP .

parameters.name: ac0singlevalue
parameters.label: Initial Value
parameters.description: Specifies a single value that all atomic counters in this binding will be initialized to.

parameters.name: ac0chopvalue
parameters.label: Initial Values  CHOP
parameters.description: A reference to the CHOP that will determine the initial values of the atomic counters in this binding. The CHOP will be spanned in track order, so the values from the first track will be read in order first, then the next track (if there is one) and so on. If there are more initial values to fill than there are values in the CHOP then they will all be set to 0. Atomic counters will be initialized from low to high offsets.

parameters.name: const
parameters.label: Constant
parameters.description: Sequence of constant uniforms

parameters.name: const0name
parameters.label: Name
parameters.description: The constant name, as declared in the shader.

parameters.name: const0value
parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The value to give the constant.

parameters.name: buffer0pop
parameters.label: POP
parameters.description: The path to the POP to get the attribute buffer from.

parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.name: resmult
parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this TOP is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working Color Space before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: srgb
parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.description: Rec.601 with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec709
parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.description: Rec.709 color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020 color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.description: DCI-P3 color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim" color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.description: 1 - ACES 2065-1 (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acescg
parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.name: useparent
parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.description: Will use the Reference White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use Parent ' selected, then 'UI Reference White' will be used.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: ui
parameters.label: UI
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI Reference White Nits' value for it's brightness.

TOP.name: hSVAdjustTOP
TOP.description: The HSV Adjust TOP adjust color values using hue, saturation, and value controls. If you change the Hue Offset, Saturation Multiplier and Value Multiplier without changing any of the other parameters then you will modify the color of all pixels in the image. The other parameters are used to narrow the range of pixels you want to modify based on their hue, saturation and value. For example if you leave the Hue Range untouched but reduce the saturation range, you will cause the TOP to modify only pixels who fall into the new saturation range. The range is the Start Color's saturation + the Range + the Falloff, in this example. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: startcolor
parameters.label: Start Color
parameters.description: ⊞ - The start color is the hue that the HSV adjustment is centered around. When adjusting a small hue range, this is the color that will be altered. In the example image above, the Start Color color is cyan with a hue value of 180.

parameters.name: huerange
parameters.label: Hue Range
parameters.description: This is the range of color from the Start Color that will be adjusted. A range of 1 will only adjust the colors that are the same as the start color. A range of 360 will adjust all colors. For example, a range of 20 and a Start Color of 180 will adjust colors in the hue range of 170-190.

parameters.name: huefalloff
parameters.label: Hue Falloff
parameters.description: This controls the falloff from the Hue Range. Higher values give more falloff, blending the hue range softly from hues that are adjusted to hues that are not.

parameters.name: saturationrange
parameters.label: Saturation Range
parameters.description: This is the range of saturation to adjust from the saturation of the Start Color. The Range is from 0 to 1.

parameters.name: saturationfalloff
parameters.label: Saturation Falloff
parameters.description: This controls the falloff from the Saturation Range selected.

parameters.name: valuerange
parameters.label: Value Range
parameters.description: This is the range of value to adjust from the value of the Start Color. The Range is from 0 to 1.

parameters.name: valuefalloff
parameters.label: Value Falloff
parameters.description: This controls the falloff from the Value Range selected.

parameters.name: hueoffset
parameters.label: Hue Offset
parameters.description: Adjust the hues selected above. The Hue Offset ranges from 0 to 360. For example, if the initial pixel color is 180 then a Hue Offset of 100 will change the hue of 180 (cyan) to be a hue of 280 (violet).

parameters.name: saturationmult
parameters.label: Saturation Multiplier
parameters.description: Adjusts the saturations selected above. This will multiply the saturation values specified by Saturation Range and Falloff parameters above. Setting this to 0 will reduce the selected saturation to 0, setting it to 1 will maintain the current saturation values, and setting it to 2 will make the selected saturation twice as saturated.

parameters.name: valuemult
parameters.label: Value Multiplier
parameters.description: Adjusts the values selected above. This will multiply the values specified by Value Range and Falloff parameters above.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

The resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer is used as the composite's final resolution and aspect ratio unless manually on the Common Page .

parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretch/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the best possible match that does not crop any of the Overlay layer. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: fitoutside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the worst possible match. This is the opposite of Best Fit. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Overlay is not squashed or stretched. The Overlay layer uses its own resolution and aspect ratio during the composite. Pixel accurate composites require Native Resolution , use this setting for to maintain an image's original resolution during the composite.

TOP.name: kinectAzureSelectTOP
TOP.description: NOTE OS: This operator is only supported under the Microsoft Windows 10 April 2018 or newer operating system. The Kinect Azure Select TOP can be used to capture additional images from a Microsoft Kinect Azure or Kinect compatible Orbbec camera that is controlled by a Kinect Azure TOP . This TOP must be used along with a Kinect Azure TOP .

parameters.name: active
parameters.label: Active
parameters.description: Controls whether this TOP is retrieving image data from the device. The primary Kinect Azure TOP must also be active to receive data.

parameters.name: top
parameters.label: Kinect Azure  TOP
parameters.description: The name of the primary Kinect Azure TOP that is configuring the camera. The primary TOP controls which camera the select TOP receives data from, as well as all device configuration such as resolution, framerate, etc.

parameters.name: image
parameters.label: Image
parameters.description: ⊞ - A list of available image types to capture from the device and display in this TOP . All image types have a second version that is mapped (aligned) to the image space of the other camera so that color and depth image data can be matched. The resolution of the image is controlled by the Color Resolution or Depth Mode parameters of the primary Kinect Azure TOP .

parameters.name: color
parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: An 8-bit RGBA image from the color camera.

parameters.name: colorremap
parameters.label: Color aligned to Depth
parameters.description: The color camera image remapped to align with the current depth camera image. The resolution is determined by the Depth Mode.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.label: Depth
parameters.description: A single channel 32-bit floating point depth image where pixel values measure the distance in meters from the camera. Resolution and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode parameter.

parameters.name: depthremap
parameters.label: Depth aligned to Color
parameters.description: The depth image remapped to align with the current color camera image. The resolution is determined by the Color Resolution .

parameters.name: ir
parameters.label: IR
parameters.description: A 16-bit integer infrared image captured by the depth camera. Resolution and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode.

parameters.name: irremap
parameters.label: IR aligned to Color
parameters.description: The infrared image remapped to align the current color camera image. The resolution is determined by the Color Resolution parameter.

parameters.name: playerindex
parameters.label: Player Index
parameters.description: An 8-bit single channel image that maps pixels to players that have been identified by the body tracking system. Pixel values represent the body id multiplied by 25 to improve contrast. Note: The player index map may have additional hardware requirements (CUDA capable graphics card) and may not synchronize with the color or depth images depending on current settings. The resolution is determined by the current Depth Mode.

parameters.name: playerindexremap
parameters.label: Player Index aligned to Color
parameters.description: The player index map remapped to align with the current color image. The resolution is determined by the Color Resolution parameter.

parameters.name: pointcloud
parameters.label: Point Cloud
parameters.description: A 32bit floating point RGBA image where the depth information has been converted into XYZ positions that are stored in the RGB channels. Position data is represented in meters and the resolution and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode. The Point Cloud image can be viewed in 3D by activating the TOP and selecting 'View as Points' in the right-click menu, or by using the TOP as an instance source in the Geometry COMP .

parameters.name: pointcloudremap
parameters.label: Point Cloud aligned to Color
parameters.description: The point cloud image remapped to align with the current color image. Note: Remapping the image can create gaps and artifacts when view the points in 3D.

parameters.name: remapimage
parameters.label: Align Image to Other Camera
parameters.description: When enabled, the current image will be remapped to align with images from the other camera. For example, use this feature to create a color camera image that maps to the pixels of the depth camera. The current depth mode and color resolution will be used to do the remapping. Note: Remapping the point cloud image can create artifacts in the distribution of points due to gaps in the remapping algorithm.

parameters.name: bodyimage
parameters.label: Sync Image to Body Tracking
parameters.description: When enabled, the image produced will be delayed so that it corresponds to the most recent data from the body tracking system.

parameters.name: mirrorimage
parameters.label: Mirror Image
parameters.description: Flip the image in the horizontal axis.

parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. TOP.name: kinectAzureTOP
TOP.description: NOTE OS: This operator is only supported under the Microsoft Windows 10 April 2018 or newer operating system. The Kinect Azure TOP can be used to configure and capture data from a Microsoft Kinect Azure camera or a Kinect compatible Orbbec camera (Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, etc). The TOP can be used to configure the settings of the camera (resolution, frame rate, synchronization, etc) as well to retrieve captured images from either its color or depth cameras. Image data from one camera can be remapped (aligned) to the other camera in order to match color and depth information. Only one Kinect Azure TOP can be connected to a single Kinect camera. To retrieve additional images from the same camera, use a Kinect Azure Select TOP . The Kinect Azure can also extract body tracking information and skeleton positions using the depth camera image. To access this data, use a Kinect Azure CHOP and set its Kinect TOP parameter to the primary Kinect Azure TOP that is connected to the device. Note: While both Microsoft and Orbbec hardware can be used in the same project, only one hardware type can have body tracking enabled at any one time. Body tracking is required for the Player Index image or to obtain skeleton data. If body tracking is not required from the Orbbec, it is recommended to use the native Orbbec TOP instead. Note: The Orbbec Femto Mega does not automatically support ethernet connections using the Kinect Azure TOP or CHOP . However, you can enable detection of ethernet devices using an external configuration file places alongside your toe file. Ethernet connections only support depth and IR images, color video is only supported over USB. For further information on the file see the Orbbec documentaion . Warning: When working with Orbbec hardware, using both Kinect Azure and Orbbec nodes in the same project may lead to instability. It is recommended to use either all Kinect Azure or all Orbbec nodes depending on project requirements. TIP: See Elburz' video on using KinectAzure's point clouds and a bunch of Azure general tips. Kinect Azure Point Cloud in TouchDesigner Tutorial on the Interactive and Immersive HQ. See also Kinect Azure CHOP , Kinect Azure Select TOP , Palette:pointRender , Palette:kinectCalibration , Palette:kinectRecorder , Palette:kinectPointcloud .

parameters.name: active
parameters.label: Active
parameters.description: Enable or disable the camera. Note Disabling this TOP will also disable any other operators ( Kinect Azure Select TOP or Kinect Azure CHOP ) that rely on it.

parameters.name: library
parameters.label: Hardware Type
parameters.description: ⊞ - Choose whether you are using Microsoft Kinect Azure hardware or a Kinect compatible Orbbec camera (Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, etc). Both camera types can be used together in the same project, but only one hardware type can enable body tracking at any one time.

parameters.name: microsoft
parameters.label: Microsoft Kinect Azure
parameters.description: Select this option if you are using an original Microsoft Kinect Azure camera.

parameters.name: orbbec
parameters.label: Orrbec Compatible (Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, ...)
parameters.description: Selection this option for a Kinect compatible Orbbec camera e.g. Femto Mega, Femto Bolt, etc. Not all Orbbec cameras are compatible with the Kinect Azure. For general Orbbec support use an Orbbec TOP .

parameters.name: sensor
parameters.label: Sensor
parameters.description: The serial number of the connected Kinect Azure camera. The TOP will automatically fill the list with all available cameras. Note: Only one Kinect Azure TOP should be connected to a single camera.

parameters.name: fps
parameters.label: Camera  FPS
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls the frame rate of both the color and depth cameras. Some higher camera resolutions are not supported when running at 30FPS. Lower framerates can produce brighter color images in low light conditions.

parameters.name: colorres
parameters.label: Color  Resolution
parameters.description: ⊞ - The resolution of images captured by the color camera. Different resolutions may have different aspect ratios. Note: 4096 x 3072 is not supported at 30 FPS .

parameters.name: 4096x3072
parameters.label: 4096 x 3072 (4x3)
parameters.description: Note: This resolution is not supported when operating at 30FPS. Reduce the framerate to 15 or 5 FPS to use this setting.

parameters.name: depthmode
parameters.label: Depth Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - The depth mode controls which of the Kinect's two depth cameras (Wide or Narrow FOV) are used to produce the depth image and whether any 'binning' is used to process the data. In 'binned' modes, 2x2 blocks of pixels are combined to produce a filter, lower resolution image. Note: Body tracking is not supported when using the Passive IR depth mode.

parameters.label: Narrow FOV
parameters.description: Unbinned (640x576) narrowunbinned -

parameters.label: Wide FOV
parameters.description: 2x2 Binned (512x512) widebinned -

parameters.name: narrowbinned
parameters.label: Narrow FOV - 2x2 Binned (320x288)
parameters.description: Note: This mode is not recommended for use with body tracking.

parameters.name: wideunbinned
parameters.label: Wide FOV - Unbinned (1024x1024)
parameters.description: Note: This mode is not supported at 30FPS and is not recommended for use with body tracking.

parameters.name: passiveir
parameters.label: Passive IR (1024x1024)
parameters.description: Note: This mode does not support body tracking.

parameters.name: modelpath
parameters.label: Body Tracking Model
parameters.description: The file path to the ONNX model that performs body tracking features. TouchDesigner includes the regular and lite models that are part of the Kinect Azure SDK.

parameters.name: proccessingmode
parameters.label: Body Tracking Processing Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the body tracking model is processed. The default mode runs mostly on the GPU (supports Nvidia, AMD and Intel), but this can also be switched to a CPU mode when a compatible GPU is not available.

parameters.name: gpudefault
parameters.label: GPU  Default
parameters.description: The default processing mode. It is equivalent to DirectML when running on Windows.

parameters.name: cpu
parameters.label: CPU
parameters.description: The AI model will run on the CPU instead of the graphics cards. This is notably slower and not recommended for production release.

parameters.name: directml
parameters.label: DirectML
parameters.description: Equivalent to the default mode when running on Windows. The AI model will run on the GPU . This is compatible with Nvidia, AMD and Intel GPUs.

parameters.name: gpu
parameters.label: Body Tracking  GPU  Device
parameters.description: The device number of the GPU to use when there are multiple GPUs in the system. The ordering system may be dependent on the GPU manufacturer.

parameters.name: orientation
parameters.label: Sensor Orientation
parameters.description: ⊞ - Used to indicate when the camera is mounted in a non-upright position. This can help improve body-tracking results.

parameters.name: image
parameters.label: Image
parameters.description: ⊞ - A list of available image types to capture from the device and display in this TOP . All image types have a second version that is mapped (aligned) to the image space of the other camera so that color and depth image data can be matched. The resolution of the image is controlled by the Color Resolution or Depth Mode parameters depending on the type of image selected. Use a Kinect Azure Select TOP to access additional image types from the same camera.

parameters.name: color
parameters.label: Color
parameters.description: An 8-bit RGBA image from the color camera.

parameters.name: colorremap
parameters.label: Color aligned to Depth
parameters.description: The color camera image remapped to align with the current depth camera image. The resolution is determined by the Depth Mode.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.label: Depth
parameters.description: A single channel 32bit floating point depth image where pixel values measure the distance in meters from the camera. Resolution and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode parameter.

parameters.name: depthremap
parameters.label: Depth aligned to Color
parameters.description: The depth image remapped to align with the current color camera image. The resolution is determined by the Color Resolution parameter.

parameters.name: ir
parameters.label: IR
parameters.description: A 16-bit integer infrared image captured by the depth camera. Resolution and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode.

parameters.name: irremap
parameters.label: IR aligned to Color
parameters.description: The infrared image remapped to align the current color camera image. The resolution is determined by the Color Resolution parameter.

parameters.name: playerindex
parameters.label: Player Index
parameters.description: An 8-bit single channel image that maps pixels to players that have been identified by the body tracking system. Pixel values represent the body id multiplied by 25 to improve contrast. Note: The player index map may have additional hardware requirements (CUDA capable graphics card) and may not synchronize with the color or depth images depending on current settings. The resolution is determined by the current Depth Mode.

parameters.name: playerindexremap
parameters.label: Player Index aligned to Color
parameters.description: The player index map remapped to align with the current color image. The resolution is determined by the Color Resolution parameter.

parameters.name: pointcloud
parameters.label: Point Cloud
parameters.description: A 32bit floating point RGBA image where the depth information has been converted into XYZ positions that are stored in the RGB channels. Position data is represented in meters and the resolution and field of view are determined by the Depth Mode. The Point Cloud image can be viewed in 3D by activating the TOP and selecting 'View as Points' in the right-click menu, or by using the TOP as an instance source in the Geometry COMP .

parameters.name: pointcloudremap
parameters.label: Point Cloud aligned to Color
parameters.description: The point cloud image remapped to align with the current color image. Note: Remapping the image can create gaps and artifacts when view the points in 3D.

parameters.name: remapimage
parameters.label: Align Image to Other Camera
parameters.description: When enabled, the current image will be remapped to align with images from the other camera. For example, use this feature to create a color camera image that maps to the pixels of the depth camera.

parameters.name: bodyimage
parameters.label: Sync Image to Body Tracking
parameters.description: When enabled, the image produced will be delayed so that it corresponds to the most recent data in the body tracking system. The amount of delay may fluctuate based on the power of the processor doing the body tracking and the complexity of the scene. A Kinect Azure Select TOP can be used at the same time to retrieve the real-time image stream.

parameters.name: mirrorimage
parameters.label: Mirror Image
parameters.description: Flip the image in the horizontal axis.

parameters.name: cpu
parameters.label: CPU Body Tracking
parameters.description: When enabled, body tracking calculations will be done on the CPU rather than on the graphics card. This method is much slower, but does not require a high-powered graphics card to function.

parameters.name: resetcolors
parameters.label: Reset Color Controls
parameters.description: Reset all of the color controls to the camera's defaults. These vary per camera and may be different than the parameter defaults.

parameters.name: enablecolors
parameters.label: Enable Color Controls
parameters.description: Turn on to enable adjustment controls for the color camera. When disabled, the previous color settings will remain in place. Use the Reset Color Controls button to switch the camera back to its default settings.

parameters.name: manualexposure
parameters.label: Manual Exposure
parameters.description: Enable to allow setting the exposure time manually. When disabled, the camera will automatically choose an exposure based on the light levels and frame rate.

parameters.name: exposure
parameters.label: Exposure Time
parameters.description: Adjust the exposure time of the color image measured in microseconds. The time must be less than one frame.

parameters.name: manualwhitebalance
parameters.label: Manual White Balance
parameters.description: Enable to allow setting the camera white balance manually.

parameters.name: whitebalance
parameters.label: White Balance
parameters.description: Select the temperature in degrees Kelvin used to set the white balance of the image. The value is rounded to the nearest 10 degrees.

parameters.name: brightness
parameters.label: Brightness
parameters.description: Used to adjust the brightness of the image from 0 to 255. 128 is the default.

parameters.name: contrast
parameters.label: Contrast

parameters.name: saturation
parameters.label: Saturation
parameters.description: Controls the saturation of the color image.

parameters.name: sharpness

parameters.name: gain

parameters.name: backlight

parameters.name: powerfreq

parameters.description: ⊞ - Select the frequency of the power supply for use in the cameras noise cancellation system.

parameters.name: depthdelay
parameters.label: Depth Image Delay
parameters.description: A delay in microseconds between when the depth and color images are captured. The delay must be less than one frame in length based on the current framerate.

parameters.name: syncmode
parameters.label: Wired Sync Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - When using more than one Kinect Azure camera, this setting can be used to determine which unit is the master and which are subordinates.

parameters.name: subdelay
parameters.label: Subordinate Delay
parameters.description: A delay in microseconds between when the master unit captures an image and when this device captures an image. (Only applicable for subordinate devices).

TOP.name: kinectTOP
TOP.description: NOTE OS: This operator is only supported under the Microsoft Windows operating system. Hardware: This TOP only supports the Kinect for Windows hardware and the Kinect 2 , not Kinect for Xbox hardware. The Kinect TOP captures video from the Kinect depth camera or RGB color camera. To use a Kinect 2 device you need to install the Kinect for Windows 2.0 SDK or runtime . To use the original Kinect 1 device you will need to install the Kinect Runtime 1.8 for builds greater than 12000, or Kinect Runtime 1.7 for builds below 12000. Kinect 2 supports color point clouds - getting the camera space positions of the color pixels, outputted as a 32-bit float RGB texture with XYZ in RGB. For use in making point clouds renders. See also Kinect CHOP , Kinect and Kinect1 .

TOP.name: layerMixTOP
TOP.description: The Layer Mix TOP lets you composite unlimited image layers and do adjustments, all within one node. Each of the inputs gets a block of parameters that you can use to modify the incoming images. The possible built-in controls per-layer include crop, pre-fit, justify, extend, scale, rotate, translate, pivot and then layer transparency, gamma and level, and finally the composite (blend) operation. To avoid clutter, on the first page you choose which controls you want to be per-layer. The entire mixing of layers is done with one single-pass shader that is generated on-the-fly. You can composite back to front, or front-to-back. You can specify a large background plate (image or constant) to composite your layers over. The background plate can be a constant-colored image with the resolution of the first input, or defined as a width-height on the Common page, or a separate TOP image. The inputs can be a mix of wired inputs and references to TOPs using pattern matching of names.

parameters.name: background
parameters.label: Background

parameters.name: off
parameters.label: Off
parameters.description: No background is used. There must be at least two layer sources provided as inputs if there is no background.

parameters.name: backgroundtop
parameters.label: Background  TOP
parameters.description: Another TOP 's output image will be used as the background.

parameters.name: constlayer
parameters.label: Constant Layer
parameters.description: A constant RGBA value will be used as the background.

parameters.name: size
parameters.label: Size
parameters.description: ⊞ - This menu determines the resolution of the output image. This parameter does not affect what gets composited, regardless of which menu item is selected. It only controls the output resolution.

parameters.name: firstinput
parameters.label: First Input
parameters.description: The resolution is the same size as the first wired input.

parameters.name: bgtopsize
parameters.label: Background  TOP
parameters.description: The resolution is the same size as another TOP 's output resolution.

parameters.name: outputres
parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.description: The resolution is defined by the Resolution parameter on the Common page.

parameters.name: bgtop
parameters.label: Background  TOP
parameters.description: The path of the Background TOP being referenced. The Background and Size parameters will share the same TOP if the Background TOP menu item is selected for both menus.

parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the red, green, blue, and alpha color channels if the Constant Layer menu item is selected for the Background parameter.

parameters.label: Enable Crop
parameters.description: Adds crop (left, right, bottom, top) parameters to each layer. If disabled, each layer will have default UV bounds of (0, 1, 0, 1).

parameters.name: cropunit
parameters.label: Crop Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the units used by the Crop parameter for each layer.

parameters.name: prefit
parameters.label: Pre-Fit Layer
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how each layer fills the composite.

parameters.name: prefitperlayer
parameters.label: Per Layer
parameters.description: Adds Pre-Fit Layer menu parameters to each layer, allowing layers to independently adjust their pre-fits.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: All layers are stretched/squashed to fill the resolution and aspect ratio of the output resolution.

parameters.name: fithorz
parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.description: All layers are stretched/squashed to fit the output resolution horizontally.

parameters.name: fitvert
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: All layers are stretched/squashed to fit the output resolution vertically.

parameters.name: fitbest
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: All layers are stretch/squashed to fit the output resolution using the best possible match that does not crop any of the layer. The aspect ratio of the layer is maintained.

parameters.name: fitoutside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: All layers are stretched squashed to fit the output resolution using the worst possible match. This is the opposite of Fit Best. The aspect ratio of the layer is maintained.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: All layers are not squashed or stretched. The layers use their own resolution and aspect ratio during the composite. Pixel accurate composites require Native Resolution . Use this setting to maintain an image's original resolution during the composite.

parameters.name: enablejust
parameters.label: Enable Justify
parameters.description: Adds justify parameters to each layer. If disabled, each layer will default to center horizontal and center vertical alignment.

parameters.name: extend
parameters.label: Extend
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the extend (or repeat) conditions of the layers. This parameter determines what happens at the edges of the layers.

parameters.name: extperlayer
parameters.label: Per Layer
parameters.description: Adds Extend menu parameters to each layer, allowing layers to independently adjust their extend conditions.

parameters.name: hold
parameters.label: Hold
parameters.description: The pixel values at the edges of all layers continue to extend past that edge.

parameters.name: zero
parameters.label: Zero
parameters.description: The image does not extend past the edges of all layers.

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.label: Repeat
parameters.description: The image is repeated at the edges of all layers.

parameters.name: mirror
parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.description: The image is mirrored at the edges of all layers.

parameters.name: scalemode
parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: ⊞ - Adds scale parameters to the layers.

parameters.name: off
parameters.label: Off
parameters.description: No scale parameters are added, so x and y scales are defaulted to 1.

parameters.name: uniform
parameters.label: Uniform
parameters.description: Adds a uniform scale parameter to each layer that scales the x and y axes simultaneously.

parameters.name: xy
parameters.label: XY
parameters.description: Adds an x and y scale parameter to each layer.

parameters.name: xyuniform
parameters.label: XY + Uniform
parameters.description: Adds both x and y and uniform scale parameters to each layer.

parameters.name: enabler
parameters.label: Enable Rotate
parameters.description: Adds rotation parameters to each layer. If disabled, each layer will have default rotation of 0.

parameters.name: enablet
parameters.label: Enable Translate
parameters.description: Adds translation parameters to each layer. If disabled, each layer will have default translation of 0.

parameters.name: enablep
parameters.label: Enable Pivot
parameters.description: Adds pivot parameters to each layer. If disabled, each layer will default the pivot to the center of the layer.

parameters.name: transpvtunit
parameters.label: Translate / Pivot Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the units used by the Translate and Pivot parameters for each layer.

parameters.name: enableopac
parameters.label: Enable Opacity
parameters.description: Adds opacity parameters to each layer. If disabled, each layer will have default opacity of 1. Setting a layer's opacity to 0 can be used to optimize the Layer Mix TOP to stop wired input nodes from cooking if it isn't being displayed.

parameters.name: enablebright
parameters.label: Enable Brightness
parameters.description: Adds brightness parameters to each layer. If disabled, each layer will have default brightness of 1.

parameters.name: enablelevels
parameters.label: Enable Levels
parameters.description: Adds black level and gamma parameters to each layer, using Luma Level TOP 's algorithm. If disabled, each layer will have default black level of 0 and gamma of 1.

parameters.name: operand
parameters.label: Operation / Swap
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the composite (blend) operation and swap order for the layers.

parameters.name: operand
parameters.label: Operation / Swap
parameters.description: If set to Per Layer, it will add Operation / Swap parameters to each layer. If set to a blend operation, this parameter will apply the operation to all layers.

parameters.name: swaporder
parameters.label: Swap Order
parameters.description: Swaps the order of all input pairs. A operation B is changed to B operation A. Operations like Add don't matter, but many do, like Over and Hard Light. If the Operation parameter is set to Per Layer, each layer will have its own Swap Order parameter to allow for swapping of specific layers.

parameters.name: comporder
parameters.label: Composite Order
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the compositing order of the layers. Front to Back means the first input will be layered at the top of the compositing stack. Back to Front means the first input will be layered at the bottom of the compositing stack.

parameters.name: fronttoback
parameters.label: Front to Back
parameters.description: Compositing follows this order: (((Input_0 op_0 Input_1) op_1 Input_2) op_2 Background). If there is no background plate, op_2 and Background are ignored.

parameters.name: backtofront
parameters.label: Back to Front
parameters.description: Compositing follows this order: (Input_2 op_2 (Input_1 op_1 (Input_0 op_0 Background))). If there is no background plate, op_0 and Background are ignored.

TOP.name: layoutTOP
TOP.description: The Layout TOP positions multiple input TOPs into rows, columns, or grids. It can either fit all the TOPs into a specific resolution (determined by the Common page) by scaling the inputs, or it can scale its own resolution to be larger to accomodate the native resolution of the inputs. Each input image gets equal area of the output, and the Fit menu determines how each image fits into its designated area. Multiple inputs can be wired into the Layout TOP , or the TOP parameter can contain paths to multiple TOPs. In the final layout, the TOPs specified in the TOP parameter will appear before the TOPs of the wired inputs if both are used.

parameters.name: scaleres

When 'on' and the output resolution is 'Use Input', the Layout TOP 's resolution is the first input's resolution scaled up by number of columns horiontally, and the number of rows vertically. For example, if there are 4 input textures and the first one is 1280x720 and Align Left to Right is selected, then the grid size is 4x1 and so the final resolution will be 5120x720 (ie. (1280*4)x(720*1)). However whether off or on, each texture gets an allotted space of the same size. How the texture fits into that space is determined using the Fit parameter.

TOP.name: leapMotionTOP
TOP.description: The Leap Motion TOP gets the image from the Leap Motion controller's cameras. To enable this feature the option Allow Images must be turned on in the Leap Motion Control Panel . To connect with the device you will need to install the Ultraleap Tracking Software. For best performance, it is recommended to use the latest version Gemini drivers for Windows (v5.13.2 or greater) or MacOS (v5.14.0 or greater) that are available here: https://developer.leapmotion.com/tracking-software-download . Legacy version 2 or version 4 Orion drivers are also supported. See the API parameter details below for more information. In addition to installing the driver, TouchDesigner must also be told where to find the tracking library. Installation instructions vary depending on the operating system: On Windows: You can use the Library Folder parameter to point to the location of the LeapC.dll (Orion/Gemini) or Leap.dll (Version 2/3) files on your system. The file is installed as part of the LeapSDK and the location may vary depending on the version and options selected during installation. On MacOS: The library folder should point to the location of the Ultraleap tracking app. By default this is '/Applications/Ultraleap Hand Tracking.app' TouchDesigner will automatically find the library files inside the application's contents folder. Tip: If using Gemini V5, the Leap Motion will only work in one orientation. By default the hands enter from the bottom of the camera view, though this can be changed in setting to invert the direction. This is an important distinction between Gemini V5 and the older V2/V4 APIs which could work in either orientation. Note: TouchDesigner does not include a license to use the Leap Motion hardware or software. Make sure to check with the UltraLeap website regarding any applicable licenses that you may need for your project. See also Leap Motion , Leap Motion CHOP
