TOP.name: lensDistortTOP
TOP.description: The Lens Distort TOP applies or removes lens distortion from an image using the Brown-Conrady model . This can be used to rectify images taken from a physical camera, to apply distortion to a rendering for use in augmented reality (AR), or as a visual effect. The distortion algorithm used by the Lens Distort TOP can be broken down into three components: radial distortion, tangential distortion and the camera matrix. Radial distortion shifts pixels in the output relative to their distance from the center of the image (defined by the Optical Center parameter). Radial distortion is controlled by the k1, k2 and k3 constants, with k1 having the greatest effect and k3 the least. Positive k values create a barrel or fisheye effect as if the image was wrapped around the surface of a sphere. Negative k values will bend the image inward to create a pincushion or pillow effect. The equations for radial distortion are: x_distorted = x * (1 + k1 * r^2 + k2 * r^4 + k3 * r^6) y_distorted = y * (1 + k1 * r^2 + k2 * r^4 + k3 * r^6) where, r = distance from center Tangential distortion shifts pixels as if they were on a surface being tilted away from the camera and is controlled by the p1 and p2 parameters. p1 tilts the image up and down depending on the sign, and p2 tilts the image left and right. The equations for tangential distortion are: x_distorted = x + (2 * p1 * x * y + p2 * (r^2 + 2 * x^2)) y_distorted = y + (p1 * (r^2 + 2 * y^2) + 2 * p2 * x * y) where, r = distance from center The camera matrix is defined by the Optical Center and Focal Length parameters and is used to transform the image positions before the distortion is applied. The Optical Center values control where the center of the distortion effect is, while the Focal Length parameters act as a scale on the other effects. The camera matrix is usually represented as a 3x3 matrix: fx 0 cx 0 fy cy 0 0 1 Distortion values for a camera lens can be determined using OpenCV calibration routines or through functions for a particular camera (see kinectazureTOP class ). Barrel or Fisheye Radial Distortion, k > 0 Pillow or Pincushion Radial Distortion, k < 0 Tangential Distortion, p1 < 0 Tangential Distortion, p2 < 0 The Layout page has parameters to control how the distorted (or undistorted) image is arranged inside the output image frame. These features can be helpful to preserve parts of the input image that might otherwise be projected offscreen, to preserve input image resolution, or to establish a consistent output frame when lens distortion parameters are changing. For example, setting the Post Transform parameter to Optimal and keeping Optimal Alpha at 1, the distorted image will be scaled and shifted so that the entire input image is kept within the output frame. Switching the Layout parameter to Native Resolution , will then scale the output resolution so that no detail from the input image is lost. Attaching an Info CHOP will provide Region of Interest (ROI) bounds that can be used to crop out the original distorted image from the output image. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: invert
parameters.label: Invert Distortion
parameters.description: Reverse the lens distortion. This will *mostly* undo the distortion applied by another Lens Distort TOP with the same parameters and Inverse disabled. The lens distortion algorithm does not have a precise inverse solution, so an approximate method is used which may not match the original image precisely. The quality of the approximation varies depending on the magnitude of the distortion. Additionally, the approximation aglorithm does not use the k3 constant and any content that was lost outside the bounds of the image cannot be recreated.

parameters.name: k1
parameters.label: K1
parameters.description: The first radial distortion constant. The k constants move pixels towards or away from the center of the image. Values greater than 0 produce a barrel or fisheye effect, while values less than zero produce a pillow or pincushion effect. k1 has a larger effect than k3.

parameters.name: k2
parameters.label: K2
parameters.description: The second radial distortion constant. See K1.

parameters.name: p1
parameters.label: P1
parameters.description: The first tangential distortion constant. Tilts the image up and down.

parameters.name: p2
parameters.label: P2
parameters.description: The second tangential distortion constant. Tilts the image left or right.

parameters.name: k3
parameters.label: K3
parameters.description: The third radial distortion constant (not used in the inverse distortion). See K1.

parameters.name: center
parameters.label: Optical Center
parameters.description: ⊞ - The position in the image that should be the center of the distortion. Depending on the unit mode selected, the position can be entered as an absolute position measured from the bottom-left corner, or as a relative position measured from the center of the image. The unit mode also controls whether the position is measured in pixels or normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: relative
parameters.label: R
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in normalized coordinates from -0.5 to -0.5 relative to the center of the image.

parameters.name: absolute
parameters.label: A
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in normalized coordinates (0 to 1) from the bottom-left corner of the image.

parameters.name: pixelrel
parameters.label: RP
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in pixel coordinates relative to the center of the image.

parameters.name: pixelabs
parameters.label: AP
parameters.description: The optical center is measured in absolute pixel coordinates from the bottom-left corner of the image.

parameters.name: focallength
parameters.label: Focal Lengths
parameters.description: ⊞ - The focal length components of the camera matrix descibed either as normalized resolution-independent values or as pixels. The focal length acts as a scalar on the other distortion parameters. The normalized unit mode can be used for systems that use millimeters or other physical units. Often abbreviated as Fx and Fy. See OpenCV for details.

parameters.name: fraction
parameters.label: F
parameters.description: The focal length is described in fractional or normalized coordinates.

parameters.name: pixels
parameters.label: P
parameters.description: The focal length is described in pixels.

parameters.name: layout
parameters.label: Layout
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the transformed image is arranged inside the final output image space. This value can be useful to preserve the native pixel resolution of the input image, or ensuring a final output resolution and aspect ratio.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.label: Scale to Fit
parameters.description: The transformed image is scaled to fill the full resolution and aspect ratio of the output image. This mode is useful if you want a specific output resolution or aspect ratio.

parameters.name: native
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: The transformed image is arranged in the output in a way that preserves its original resolution and aspect ratio. This may mean the image is cropped if the output resolution is smaller than the input resolution.

parameters.name: extendmode
parameters.label: Extend Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines what values are used when the output image exceeds the bounds of the input image.

parameters.name: hold
parameters.label: Hold
parameters.description: Colors from the outside edge of the input image are extended to fill any gaps in the output image.

parameters.name: zero
parameters.label: Zero
parameters.description: Empty gaps in the output image are filled with zeroes in all channels.

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.label: Repeat
parameters.description: The input image is tiled to fill gaps in the output image.

parameters.name: mirror
parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.description: The input image is mirrored and tiled to fill games in the output image.

parameters.name: alpha
parameters.label: Optimal Alpha
parameters.description: Determines how much of the image is preserved when calculating the optimal post transform. When zero, the optimal transform will include only the region of interest. When one, the transform will include all of the pixels from the input image. This value is equivalent to the 'alpha' value used in OpenCVs getOptimalNewCameraMatrix function.

parameters.name: transformmode
parameters.label: Post Transform
parameters.description: ⊞ - Choose whether to preform an addition transformation to the image after the lens distortion is applied. This is useful for positioning and scaling the distorted image within the final image frame and can be used to preserve parts of the input image that would be shifted out of frame by the distortion.

parameters.name: none
parameters.label: None
parameters.description: No additional transformation is applied.

parameters.name: optimal
parameters.label: Optimal
parameters.description: The image is transformed according to the optimal new camera matrix as given by OpenCVs getOptimalNewCamera matrix. Depending on the value of the Optimal Alpha parameter, this mode can be used to ensure that none of the input image is lost outside of the image frame.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom
parameters.description: Enables the custom center and scaling parameters. Use this option to modify the output image relative to the camera matrix on the Lens Distort page.

parameters.name: newmatrix
parameters.label: New Camera Matrix
parameters.description: Enter a new camera matrix for positioning the output image within the frame. Entering the camera matrix values from the Lens Distort page will result in no further transformation. Entering the optimal new camera matrix values will produce the same results as using the Optimal transform mode.

parameters.name: newcenter
parameters.label: New Center
parameters.description: ⊞ - A new optical center position that allows for shifting the transformed image within the output image frame. Using the same value as the Optical Center parameter will result in no post distortion offset. Using the Optimal Center value will produce the same results as the Optimal transform mode.

parameters.name: newcenterunit
parameters.label: New Center Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the new center values are interpreted.

parameters.name: relative
parameters.label: R
parameters.description: The center is measured in normalized coordinates from -0.5 to -0.5 relative to the center of the image.

parameters.name: absolute
parameters.label: A

parameters.name: pixelrel
parameters.label: RP

parameters.name: pixelabs
parameters.label: AP
parameters.description: The center is measured in absolute pixel coordinates from the bottom-left corner of the image.

parameters.name: newfocallength

Using the same value as the Focal Lengths parameter will result in no post distortion scaling. Using the Optimal Focal Length value will produce the same results as the Optimal transform mode.

parameters.name: fraction
parameters.label: F

parameters.name: pixels
parameters.label: P
parameters.description: The focal length is described in pixels.

parameters.name: centeroffset
parameters.label: Center Offset
parameters.description: ⊞ - Shifts the distorted image within the output image frame.

parameters.label: F
parameters.description: The offset amount is measured as a fraction of the output image from -0.5 to 0.5.

parameters.name: pixels
parameters.label: P
parameters.description: The offset amount is measured in pixels of the input image.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.label: Scale
parameters.description: ⊞ - Performs an additional post-distortion scale on the image. The scale is relative to the original camera matrix, so values greater than 1 will stretch the image, while values less than 1 will shrink it.

parameters.name: cropmode
parameters.label: Cropping
parameters.description: ⊞ - Crop the transformed image so that only part of the image will appear in the final output. Unless a custom resolution is given, the cropped region will be used to determine the final output resolution.

parameters.name: none
parameters.label: None
parameters.description: No cropping is done.

parameters.name: roi
parameters.label: Region of Interest
parameters.description: The region of interest (ROI), as defined by the OpenCV function getNewCameraMatrix, is used to crop the final output. The ROI is automatically updated by any post transform functions, so this mode will still work when using a custom transform; however, cropping the ROI from a transformed image will generally produce the same result as using no transform or crop.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom
parameters.description: Enter custom cropping region in pixels or as a fraction of the frame. Entering the ROI values from an attached Info CHOP will produce the same results as using the Region of Interest cropping mode.

parameters.name: cropregion
parameters.label: Custom Region
parameters.description: ⊞ - Defines a custom cropping region in the order of Left, Bottom, Right, Top. The values can either be as a fraction of the image (0-1) or as pixels of the input image size. Entering the ROI values from an attached Info CHOP will produce the same results as using the Region of Interest cropping mode.

parameters.name: cropregionx

parameters.name: cropregiony

parameters.name: cropregionz

parameters.name: cropregionw

parameters.name: cropunit

parameters.name: nativeres

parameters.name: filtertype

parameters.name: nearest

parameters.name: linear

parameters.name: mipmap

TOP.name: levelTOP
TOP.description: The Level TOP adjusts image contrast, brightness, gamma, black level, color range, quantization, opacity and more. See also the Luma Level TOP which preserves hue and saturation more accurately, but is slower. The Level TOP 's features have been built into one TOP to maximize performance in a single pass. It takes all its parameters to make a lookup table on the CPU, so animating parameters in the Level TOP will decrease its performance as the lookup table is recreated each frame that a parameter changes. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: clampinput

parameters.name: blacklevel

parameters.name: brightness1
parameters.label: Brightness 1
parameters.description: Increases or decreases the brightness of an image. Brightness can be considered the arithmetic mean of the RGB channels. The Brightness parameter adds or subtracts an offset into the R, G, and B channels. Low brightness will result in dark tones, while high brightness will wash the color out towards white.

parameters.name: gamma1
parameters.label: Gamma 1
parameters.description: The Gamma parameter applies a gamma correction to the image. Gamma is the relationship between the brightness of a pixel as it appears on the screen, and the numerical value of that pixel. This is often represented by a gamma curve. The difference between brightness and gamma is that gamma also affects the ratio of red to green to blue. A straight, linear gamma curve with a value of 1 means no change.

parameters.name: contrast
parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: Contrast applies a scale factor (gain) to the RGB channels. Increasing contrast will brighten the light areas and darken the dark areas of the image, making the difference between the light and dark areas of the image stronger.

TOP.name: limitTOP
TOP.description: The Limit TOP can limit the pixel values of the input image to fall between a minimum and maximum value, and can quantize the pixels by value or position. Limiting a channel causes all of its values to lie within the given range. Several different methods are available to determine what happens to values outside of the Minimum/Maximum range. Quantizing pixel values will snap each channel to the closest allowable value (the "quantized values"). Quantizing methods are: Floor, Ceiling, and Round. Quantizing pixel positions will cause all pixels within the quantization step to take the same value. This is equivalent to lowering the image resolution and then scaling the image back to its original size with no filtering applied. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: minop

parameters.description: ⊞ - The wrapping method used when applying limits to the pixel values in the image.

parameters.name: off
parameters.label: Off
parameters.description: No limits are applied to the pixel values.

parameters.name: clamp
parameters.label: Clamp
parameters.description: Pixel values are constrained to the ranged defined by the Minimum and Maximum parameters. Values outside of the range are replaced with the Minimum or Maximum value.

parameters.name: loop
parameters.label: Loop
parameters.description: Values outside of the Minimum/Maximum range continue at the other end of the interval e.g. as values go above the Maximum they loop back and start again at the Minimum value.

parameters.name: zigzag
parameters.label: Zig Zag
parameters.description: When values go beyond the Minimum or Maximum values they mirror back towards the other end of the range e.g. when a value goes above the maximum it flips and starts going back to the minimum.

parameters.name: maxop
parameters.label: Maximum Function
parameters.description: ⊞ - The wrapping method used when applying limits to the pixel values in the image.

TOP.name: lookupTOP
TOP.description: The Lookup TOP replaces color values in the TOP image connected to its first input with values derived from a lookup table created from its second input or a lookup table created using the CHOP parameter. When using the 2nd input, the lookup table is created by defining a line (start and end position) on the TOP image. When using a CHOP the lookup table is created directly from the CHOP 's values and the 2nd input is ignored. The Index Range parameter can be used to define the minimum and maximum index values that will map to the first and last values in the lookup table. When the index goes outside of this range, it will hold on the first or last value of the lookup table. For example if the range is set to [0.1, 0.2], a value from the first texture of 0.15 will map to the middle of the lookup. A value of 0.1 (and below) will map to the dark end of the lookup and a value of 0.2 (and above) will map to the light end of the lookup. See also Remap TOP , Displace TOP . Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: method
parameters.label: Method
parameters.description: ⊞ - Choose to use a line from the 2nd input (defined using UV coordinates) or CHOP values to define the lookup table.

parameters.name: secondinput
parameters.label: 2nd Input, UV Coordinates
parameters.description: Use the Dark UV and Light UV parameters to define the lookup table as a line extrated from the 2nd input.

parameters.name: chop
parameters.label: CHOP  Values
parameters.description: Use a CHOP referenced in th CHOP parameter to define the lookup table.

parameters.name: index
parameters.label: Index Range
parameters.description: ⊞ - The Index Range maps the index values to the lookup table's start and end and defaults to 0 and 1. The first parameter represents the start of the lookup table. When the index color has this value, it will index the start of the lookup table. The second parameter represents the end of the lookup table and behaves in the same way. Note: When the index goes outside of this range, it will hold on the first or last value of the lookup table.

parameters.label: index1
parameters.description: The minimum index value that maps to the start of the lookup table. Indices below this value will hold on the first value of the lookup table.

parameters.label: index2
parameters.description: The maximum index value that maps to the end of the lookup table. Indices above this value will hold on the last value of the lookup table.

parameters.name: channel
parameters.label: Index  Channel
parameters.description: ⊞ - The Index Channel controls how the color from the input is turned into a index to do the lookup. By default, the RGBA Independent option will do a separate lookup in each channel i.e. the red output channel will be based on the red value in the lookup table and the red value in the index image. For other options, like Luminance or RGBA Average, a single index value is calculated from the index color and all channels of the output image will be taken from the same pixel of the lookup table at the given index.

parameters.name: independentalpha
parameters.label: Independent Alpha
parameters.description: When enabled, the Alpha value of the output image is retrieved independently from the lookup table based on the alpha channel of the index image (the first input). This option can reproduce the legacy behavior of using the luminance to lookup the RGB values while using the alpha to separately lookup the alpha value. This option has no effect if using the 'RGBA Independent' or 'Alpha' index channel options since those modes already use the alpha channel as an index.

parameters.name: darkuv
parameters.label: Dark UV
parameters.description: ⊞ - Set the UV position to use for dark end of the lookup table. In the original image connected to the first input, any pixel with a value of (0,0,0) will be replaced by the value found at this UV position in the image connected to the second input.

parameters.name: lightuv
parameters.label: Light UV
parameters.description: ⊞ - Set the UV position to use for light end of the lookup table. In the original image connected to the first input, any pixel with a value of (1,1,1) will be replaced by the value found at this UV position in the image connected to the second input.

parameters.name: chop
parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.description: Reference the CHOP to use to define the RGBA (A is optional) values in the lookup table.

parameters.name: clampchopvalues
parameters.label: Clamp  CHOP  Values
parameters.description: Clamps CHOP values between 0-1.

parameters.name: displaylookup
parameters.label: Output Lookup
parameters.description: Outputs the lookup table itself, instead of replacing the color values of the first input.

TOP.name: lumaBlurTOP
TOP.description: The Luma Blur TOP blurs image on a per-pixel basis depending on the luminance or greyscale value of its second input. The image is blurred with separate parameters for white and black filter sizes, which correspond to the white and black luminance values of the second input. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: bartlette

parameters.name: sinc

parameters.name: hanning

parameters.name: blackman

TOP.name: lumaLevelTOP
TOP.description: The Luma Level TOP adjusts image brightness, gamma, black level, quantization, opacity and more. It has similar parameters to the Level TOP , but it maintains the hue and saturation more accurately when you use Gamma and Black Level. In the Level TOP , lowering the gamma will raise the saturation and shift the hue. Luma Level preserves saturation and hue. It also includes a Source parameter which allows the level adjustment to be applied only to certain parts of the image. For example, if source is set to Luminance, then the adjustments made with the Luma Level's parameters will be applied to the luminance of the image (ie. Invert = 1 would invert the luminance of the image, not the color). Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.label: Invert
parameters.description: Inverts the colors in the image. Black becomes white, white becomes black. Colors invert across the color wheel, so red becomes cyan, blue becomes yellow, green becomes magenta, and so on.

parameters.name: blacklevel
parameters.label: Black Level
parameters.description: Any pixel with a value less than or equal to this will be black.

parameters.name: brightness1
parameters.label: Brightness 1
parameters.description: Increases or decreases the brightness of an image. Brightness can considered the arithmetic mean of the RGB channels. The Brightness parameter adds of subtracts an offset into the R, G, and B channels. Low brightness will result in dark tones, while high brightness will wash the color out towards white.

parameters.name: gamma1
parameters.label: Gamma 1
parameters.description: The Gamma parameter applies a gamma correction to the image. Gamma is the relationship between the brightness of a pixel as it appears on the screen, and the numerical value of that pixel. This is often represented by a gamma curve. The difference between brightness and gamma is that gamma also effects the ratio of red to green to blue. A straight, linear gamma curve with a value of 1 means no change.

parameters.name: contrast
parameters.label: Contrast
parameters.description: Contrast applies a scale factor (gain) to the RGB channels. Increasing contrast will brighten the light areas and darken the dark areas of the image, making the difference between the light and dark areas of the image stronger.

parameters.label: In Low

parameters.description: Take the negative value of each input value.

parameters.name: pos

parameters.name: inverse

TOP.name: movieFileInTOP
TOP.description: The Movie File In TOP loads movies, still images, or a sequence of still images into TOPs. It will read images in .jpg , .gif , .tif , or .bmp format. It will read movies in QuickTime's .mov format, .mp4 , .mpg , .mpeg , .avi , .wmv , .dpx , Cineform and Hap Q formats (including Hap Q with Alpha). It also supports the NotchLC codec, EXR files ( .exr ) and some .swf and .flv Flash files as well as DXT1/3/5 and RG compressed .dds files. Images and movies can also be fetched from the web by using http:// to specify a URL. Access the hardware decoder on Nvidia GPUs with the Hardware Decode parameter on the 'Tune' page. This supports 10 and 12-bit H264/H265s and YUV 444 files on supporting hardware, converted into 16-bit pixel channels. Other codecs that this also decodes include VP8, VP9, JPEG, AV1, VC1. More information here. When reading file formats that support higher bit depths such as 10-bit/16-bit/32-bit, an appropriate pixel format will be automatically used as long as the 'Pixel Format' menu on the Common page is left as 'Use Input'. i.e. a 16-bit file will cause each pixel to have 16-bits per color channel automatically. For a complete list, see File Types . Examine the state of a Movie File In TOP by attaching an Info CHOP to it (see below on Info CHOP ). This will show info like movie length, resolution, the number of images per second (the sample_rate channel), and whether there is audio in the file. It also shows dynamic information like movie open status, current frame, readahead frames and queue size, dropped frame count, CPU decode time and GPU upload time. Note that a movie's "images per second" (sample_rate) may be different than the timeline's frames per second. When referring to the movie's "index", it's in reference to the sequence of images in the movie file, not related to the global project frame rate. See also the page on Movie File In TOP optimizations Movie Playback , plus Hap , Movie File Out TOP , Cineform and Video Stream In TOP .

parameters.label: File
parameters.description: The path and name of the image or movie file to load. Image and movie formats are those found in File Types . You can specify files on the internet using http:// ...

parameters.description: ⊞ - Change from 0 to 1 to force the image to reload, useful when the file changes or did not exist at first.

parameters.name: reloadpulse
parameters.label: Reload  Pulse
parameters.description: Instantly reloads the file.

parameters.name: playmode
parameters.label: Play Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - Specifies the method used to play the movie, there are 3 options.

parameters.name: locked
parameters.label: Locked to  Timeline
parameters.description: This mode locks the movie position to the timeline. Scrubbing or jumping in the timeline will change the movie position accordingly. The parameters Play, Reset, Speed, and Index are disabled in this mode since the timeline is directly tied to movie position.

parameters.name: specify
parameters.label: Specify Index
parameters.description: This mode allows the user to specify a particular position in the movie using the Index parameter below. Use this mode for random access to any location in the movie.

parameters.name: sequential
parameters.label: Sequential
parameters.description: This mode continually plays regardless of the timeline position (the Index parameter is disabled). Reset and Speed parameters below are enabled to allow some control.

parameters.name: timecodeop
parameters.label: Timecode  Object / CHOP / DAT
parameters.description: This mode allows the user to set the movie index by reference to a timecode in the form of either a CHOP , DAT , or Timecode Class object.

parameters.name: play
parameters.label: Play
parameters.description: Movie plays when 1, movie stops when 0.

parameters.name: speed
parameters.label: Speed
parameters.description: This is a speed multiplier which only works when Play Mode is Sequential . A value of 1 is the default playback speed. A value of 2 is double speed, 0.5 is half speed and so on. Negative values will play the movie backwards.

parameters.name: cue
parameters.label: Cue
parameters.description: ⊞ - Jumps to Cue Point when set to 1. Only available when Play Mode is Sequential.

parameters.name: cuepoint
parameters.label: Cue  Point
parameters.description: ⊞ - Set any index in the movie as a point to jump to.

parameters.name: cuepulse
parameters.label: Cue  Pulse
parameters.description: Instantly jumps to the Cue Point position in the movie.

parameters.name: cuebehavior
parameters.label: Cue Behavior
parameters.description: ⊞ - Customize the Cue parameter's behavior.

parameters.name: repeat
parameters.label: On Release, Repeat Cued  Frame
parameters.description: When releasing the Cue parameter, immediately play the next frame.

parameters.name: play
parameters.label: On Release, Play Next  Frame
parameters.description: When releasing the Cue parameter, first play the cued frame before continuing to play the next frame.

parameters.name: index
parameters.label: Index
parameters.description: ⊞ - This parameter explicitly sets the movie position when Play Mode is set to Specify Index. The units menu on the right lets you specify the index in the following units: Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage). For example, assume you have a movie that internally is 25 fps, and the timeline that is 60 fps. If you set Units to Index and the parameter value to 25, you get the image that is 1 second into the movie. If you set the Units to Frames and set the value to 60 you get the same image at 1 second into the movie. When this number is negative the index will cycle back through the movie.

parameters.name: cuepointunit
parameters.label: Cue Point Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.name: loopcrossfade
parameters.label: Loop Crossfade
parameters.description: ⊞ - Crossfades the beginning and end of the movie together to create a smooth transition when looping. If the movie uses Trim options, it will crossfade Trim Start with Trim End positions.

parameters.name: stepsize
parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.description: Sets how many frames to skip before displaying next frame. For example, a StepSize of 30 will display every 30th frame. This timing of movie playback does not change, so with a Step Size of 30 and a sample rate of 30, a new frame will be displayed every second.

parameters.name: audioloop
parameters.label: Audio Loop
parameters.description: ⊞ - This menu helps you determine how to treat the audio as the end of a movie approaches. This is needed because of all the cases of playing a movie, like when driving with an index, the TOP will not know if you intend to loop it or not.

parameters.name: silence
parameters.label: Silence
parameters.description: Audio will go silent when movie ends.

parameters.name: fade
parameters.label: Fade
parameters.description: Audio will fade out when movie ends.

parameters.name: indexunit
parameters.label: Index Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.name: imageindexing
parameters.label: Image Sequence Indexing
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how an image sequence is ordered.

parameters.name: zero
parameters.label: Zero Based
parameters.description: Index the sequence of images starting at 0, after sorting them alphanumerically.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.label: Filename Based
parameters.description: Index the sequence of images using the numbers on the end of the filenames. I.e a file named flower400.tiff will be frame index 400, regardless of if there are other files in the directory before it.

parameters.name: loopcrossfadeunit
parameters.label: Loop Crossfade Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.name: timecodeop
parameters.label: Timecode  Object / CHOP / DAT
parameters.description: Set the movie index with a reference to a timecode. Should be a reference to either a CHOP with channels 'hour', 'second', 'minute', 'frame', a DAT with a timecode string in its first cell, or a Timecode Class object.

parameters.name: interp
parameters.label: Interpolate Frames
parameters.description: Interpolates between frames based based on exact time. For example, if the index (in frames) is 1.5, then frames 1 and 2 will be blended 50-50. If the index is 1.7 then 30% of frame 1 is blended with 70% of frame 2 and so on.

parameters.name: deinterlace
parameters.label: Deinterlace
parameters.description: ⊞ - For movies that are stored as fields, where each image is made of two images interleaved together. A 30-frame per second movie would contain 60 fields per second. For each image, the even scanlines of the first field are interleaved with the odd scanlines of the second field. The Movie File In TOP has several ways of dealing with this:

parameters.name: off
parameters.label: Off
parameters.description: Output the movie images unchanged.

parameters.name: even
parameters.label: Even
parameters.description: Take only the even scanlines of the file's images and create the odd scanlines by interpolating between the even scanlines. (For historic reasons, scanline 0 is at the top of the images for the purpose of the deinterlacing.)

parameters.name: precedence
parameters.label: Field Precedence
parameters.description: ⊞ - Where fields are extracted one field at a time, this will extract the Even field first by default, otehrwise it will extract the odd field first. The video industry has not standardized on one or the other.

parameters.name: even
parameters.label: Even
parameters.description: When the disk files are fragmented. The Movie File In TOP will read frames of the movie into memory before they are used, this can eliminate pops or stutters in playback that occur from fragmented files, other resources accessing the hard drive, or movie looping.

parameters.name: bottomhalfalpha
parameters.label: Bottom Half is Alpha (AAA)
parameters.description: If enabled, the image/movie will have it's height halved, and the R channel from the pixels on the bottom half will be treated as if they were the alpha channel for the top half. Useful for cases where the image format does not support alpha natively.

parameters.name: premultrgbbyalpha
parameters.label: Pre-Multiply RGB by Alpha
parameters.description: ⊞ - Premultiplies the image.

parameters.name: inputcolorspace
parameters.label: Input Color Space
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls what color space the input data will be treated as. It will be converted to the Working Color Space when uploaded to the GPU .

parameters.name: automatic
parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.description: Automatically try to determine the input's color space based on color space metadata available from the input, if any. If no color space can be determined, it is assumed to be sRGB.

parameters.name: srgb
parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.description: Rec.601 with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec709
parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.description: Rec.709 color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020 color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020st2084pq
parameters.label: Rec.2020 ST2084PQ
parameters.description: Rec.2020 color space, with Perceptual Quantizer transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020hlg
parameters.label: Rec.2020 HLG
parameters.description: Rec.2020 color space, with Hybrid Log Gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.description: DCI-P3 color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim" color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: displayp3d65linear
parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65) - Linear
parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and linear transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.description: 1 - ACES 2065-1 (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acescg
parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acesproxy
parameters.label: ACESproxy
parameters.description: ACESproxy color space, which has a log transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.description: Gamma 2.4 rec709gamma24 -

parameters.name: inputreferencewhite
parameters.label: Input  Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting the input color values to the Working Color Space, this controls how they should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of the colors will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space detected/selected.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Input Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Input Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: loadingerrorimage
parameters.label: Loading/Error Image
parameters.description: ⊞ - When the file can not be loaded for some reason, select what to display instead.

parameters.name: coloredbottomright
parameters.label: Colored Bottom Right Square
parameters.description: Show a colored square in the bottom right. Red means failed to load, grey means still loading.

parameters.name: zero
parameters.label: Zero
parameters.description: Show a blank frame.

parameters.name: trim
parameters.label: Trim
parameters.description: Enables the parameters below to set trim in and out points.

parameters.name: tstart
parameters.label: Trim Start
parameters.description: ⊞ - Trim the starting point of the movie.

parameters.name: tstartunit
parameters.label: Trim Start Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.name: tend
parameters.label: Trim End
parameters.description: ⊞ - Trim the ending point of the movie.

parameters.name: tendunit
parameters.label: Trim End Unit
parameters.description: ⊞ - Select the units for this parameter from Index, Frames, Seconds, and Fraction (percentage).

parameters.name: textendleft
parameters.label: Extend Left
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the Movie File In TOP handles movie positions that lie before the Trim Start position. For example, if Trim Start is set to 1, and the movie's current index is -10, the Extend Left menu determines how the movie position is calculated.

parameters.name: hold
parameters.label: Hold
parameters.description: Displays the first frame in the movie range (the frame specified by Trim Start) for any position before Trim Start.

parameters.name: cycle
parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.description: Loops the movie range continuously.

parameters.name: mirror
parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.description: Loops the movie range in a zig-zag pattern. For example, playing backwards from Trim Start the movie will index will climb towards Trim End, at which point is will decend down towards Trim Start again and continue to zig-zag (or mirror) the further the movie plays backwards.

parameters.name: black
parameters.label: Black
parameters.description: Displays black frame for any movie position before Trim Start.

parameters.name: textendright
parameters.label: Extend Right
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the Movie File In TOP handles movie positions that lie after the Trim End position. For example, if Trim End is set to 20, and the movie's current index is 25, the Extend Right menu determines how the movie position is calculated.

parameters.name: hold
parameters.label: Hold
parameters.description: Displays the last frame in the movie range (the frame specified by Trim End) for any position after Trim End.

parameters.name: cycle
parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.description: Loops the movie range continuously.

parameters.name: mirror
parameters.label: Mirror
parameters.description: Loops the movie range in a zig-zag pattern. For example, playing forwards from Trim End the movie will index will start decending towards Trim Start, at which point is will start climbing towards Trim End and continue to zig-zag (or mirror) the further the movie plays.

parameters.name: black
parameters.label: Black
parameters.description: Displays black frame for any movie position after Trim End.

parameters.name: overridesample
parameters.label: Override  Sample Rate
parameters.description: Turn On to change the sample rate of the movie. When loading an image sequence, use these parameters to set the playback speed for the sequence.

parameters.name: samplerate
parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.description: Set the sample rate for playback when 'Override Sample Rate ' above is On.

parameters.name: prereadframes
parameters.label: Pre-Read Frames
parameters.description: Sets how many video frames TouchDesigner reads ahead and stores in memory. The Movie File In TOP will read and decode frames of the movie into CPU memory before they are used, this can eliminate pops or stutters in playback that occur from some frames taking too long to decode, other resources accessing the hard drive, or movie looping. When reading a sequence of image, having more Pre Read Frames will allow multiple images to be decode at the same time. This allows playback of heavy file formats such as .exr in real-time, assuming the machine has enough CPU cores.

parameters.name: frametimeout
parameters.label: Frame Read Timeout
parameters.description: The time (in milliseconds) TouchDesigner will wait for a frame from the hard drive before giving up. If the Disk Read Timeout time is reached, that frame is simply skipped. This also works for network files that are downloaded via http://.

parameters.name: frametimeoutstrat
parameters.label: Frame Timeout Strategy
parameters.description: ⊞ - When on, if the Disk Read Timeout is reached TouchDesigner will use the latest available frame in place of the skipped frame.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.label: Keep  Frame
parameters.description: Keep showing the same frame that is currently being output.

parameters.name: playback
parameters.label: Best for Playback
parameters.description: Try to pick the best frame for playback. This may be a newer frame that what is shown, but not quite the frame that is requested.

parameters.name: seeking
parameters.label: Best for Seeking
parameters.description: Try to show any frame, either before or after the target frame. Good for when seeking the movie via a shuttle widget in a UI.

parameters.name: alwaysloadinitial
parameters.label: Always Load Initial  Frame
parameters.description: If this parameter is turned on, then for the first loaded frame the Frame Read Timeout will be ignored, and it will always wait for the first frame to ensure the node always starts up with a valid image.

parameters.name: opentimeout
parameters.label: File Open Timeout
parameters.description: The time (in milliseconds) TouchDesigner will wait for a movie to open. If the Disk Open Timout is reached, the Movie File In TOP will stop waiting and make its image all black, with a grey square in the bottom right corner. If the file still isn't opened the next time the TOP cooks, it'll wait again, and do the same. It'll keep doing this until the file is opened, or the open fails.

parameters.name: predownloadhttp
parameters.label: Pre-Download HTTP Addresses
parameters.description: When On, the file will be fully downloaded before playing. When Off, the file will be streamed from its currently URL.

parameters.name: updateimage
parameters.label: Update Image
parameters.description: Image will not update when set to 0. Movie index will continue to move forward but the output image will not update. This is useful when you are using a Movie Audio CHOP to get audio from the movie, but you don't care about the video.

parameters.name: maxdecodecpus
parameters.label: Max Decode CPUs
parameters.description: Limit the maximum number of CPUs that will be used to decode certain video codecs that are capable of multi-CPU decoding, such as H264/H265 and Cineform. Note that this does not affect multi-threaded decoding for image sequence playback, which is instead controlled by increasing the Pre-Read Frame parameter.

parameters.name: highperfread
parameters.label: High Performance Read
parameters.description: This option should be used when playing back files that require very high SSD read speeds such as high resolution (4K+) HAP Q files. It greatly improves read performance in those cases. It should not be used for low resolution or low data rate files such as 1080p H264 files.

parameters.name: highperfreadfactor
parameters.label: High Performance Read Factor
parameters.description: When doing high performance reads, this parameter controls the size of the read operations that are done on disk. Whatever the largest operation the codec asks to be done, this is multiplied by the read factor and all subsequent reads will read that much data instead. This can result in higher throughput depending on the drives. For example if a request is made to read 1MB and the factor is set to 3, then instead the operations will read 3MB from the disk and the extra 2MB read will be ready for the next frame and will likely already have the next 2 frames available in CPU RAM.

parameters.name: hwdecode
parameters.label: Hardware Decode
parameters.description: Controls if this node should use hardware decoding via the Nvidia hardware decoder chip. You can check if hardware decoding is being used using the Info CHOP , 'hardware_decode' channel. This parameter does nothing for Hap and NotchLC codecs, which are always hardware decoded.

parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.description: ⊞ - quickly change the resolution of the TOP 's data.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.name: eighth
parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: quarter
parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: half
parameters.label: Half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 2x
parameters.label: 2X
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 4x
parameters.label: 4X
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 8x
parameters.label: 8X
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: fit
parameters.label: Fit  Resolution
parameters.description: Grow or shrink the input resolution to fit this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.label: Limit  Resolution
parameters.description: Limit the input resolution to be not larger than this resolution, while keeping the aspect ratio the same.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: ⊞ - Enabled only when the Resolution parameter is set to Custom Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.name: resmult
parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this TOP is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.name: aspect
parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.description: ⊞ - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.name: armenu
parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.description: ⊞ - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the TOP .

parameters.name: nearest
parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: linear
parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get TOP images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.description: Uses mipmap filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determine how the TOP image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.name: width
parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer horizontally.

parameters.name: height
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: Stretches image to fit viewer vertically.

parameters.name: best
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so no part of image is cropped.

parameters.name: outside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Stretches or squashes image so image fills viewer while constraining it's proportions. This often leads to part of image getting cropped by viewer.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Displays the native resolution of the image in the viewer.

parameters.name: filtertype
parameters.label: Viewer Smoothness
parameters.description: ⊞ - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.name: nearest
parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: linear
parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get TOP images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.description: Uses mipmap filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.name: npasses
parameters.label: Passes
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the TOP the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the GLSL TOP when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected TOP 's image.

parameters.name: chanmask
parameters.label: Channel Mask
parameters.description: Allows you to choose which channels (R, G, B, or A) the TOP will operate on. All channels are selected by default.

parameters.name: format
parameters.label: Pixel Format
parameters.description: ⊞ - Format used to store data for each channel in the image (ie. R, G, B, and A). Refer to Pixel Formats for more information.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's pixel format.

parameters.name: rgba8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel.

parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does not apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to sRGB .

parameters.name: rgba16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 32-bits per color channel, 128-bits per pixels.

parameters.name: rgb10a2fixed
parameters.label: 10-bit RGB, 2-bit Alpha, fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 10-bits per color channel and 2-bits for alpha, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 16-bits per color channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rgba11float
parameters.label: 11-bit float (RGB), Positive Values Only
parameters.description: A RGB floating point format that has 11 bits for the Red and Green channels, and 10-bits for the Blue Channel , 32-bits total per pixel (therefore the same memory usage as 8-bit RGBA). The Alpha channel in this format will always be 1. Values can go above one, but can't be negative. ie. the range is [0, infinite).

parameters.name: mono8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: mono32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono)
parameters.description: Single channel, where RGB will all have the same value, and Alpha will be 1.0. 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: rg8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: rg32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (RG)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, R and G have values, while B is 0 always and Alpha is 1.0. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits total per pixel.

parameters.name: a8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 8-bits per channel, 8-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 16-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: a32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (A)
parameters.description: An Alpha only format that has 32-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha8fixed
parameters.label: 8-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 8-bits per channel, 16-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha16fixed
parameters.label: 16-bit fixed (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha16float
parameters.label: 16-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 16-bits per channel, 32-bits per pixel.

parameters.name: monoalpha32float
parameters.label: 32-bit float (Mono+Alpha)
parameters.description: A 2 channel format, one value for RGB and one value for Alpha. 32-bits per channel, 64-bits per pixel.

parameters.label: index
parameters.description: The current frame index being shown. This is in the FPS of the movie file, not in timeline frames.

parameters.label: true_index
parameters.description: When the movie has a Trim applied to it, this will show the actually frame index within the movie being shown.

parameters.label: index_fraction
parameters.description: Normalized index value going from 0-1 from start to the end of the movie.

parameters.label: file_resx
parameters.description: The width of the movie in pixels.

parameters.label: file_resy
parameters.description: The height of the movie in pixels.

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Unused currently.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: The length of the movie, in movie frames.

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The FPS of the movie.

parameters.label: last_index_uploaded
parameters.description: The last movie frame uploaded to the GPU .

parameters.label: mv_has_audio
parameters.description: 1 if the movie has an audio track, 0 if not.

parameters.label: preloading
parameters.description: 1 if the movie is currently preloading via the preload() Python method.

parameters.label: odd_field
parameters.description: When deinterlacing using Bob (split), 1 means the odd field is being shown, 0 means the even field is being shown.

parameters.label: last_frame
parameters.description: 1 if the last frame of the movie is currently being shown, 0 if not. Note that if a frame is dropped the last frame may never get shown, if the movie is looping.

parameters.label: loop_frame
parameters.description: 1 if the movie has just looped.

TOP.name: movieFileOutTOP
TOP.description: The Movie File Out TOP saves a TOP stream out to a movie file ( .mov / .mp4 ) using a variety of codecs, including the H.264/H.265, Hap Q , NotchLC , Apple ProRes and Animation video codecs. It can also save single frame images, image sequences, or stop-frame movies. For codecs that support Alpha, use the 'Movie Pixel Format' parameter to select a format that includes alpha. The Export Movie Dialog is a user interface built around the Movie File Out TOP . To record movies with audio using the Movie File Out TOP , a Time Sliced CHOP with mono or stereo channels of audio is required. If TouchDesigner is running at a lower frame rate than the target video frame rate and a CHOP is specified for audio, the Movie File Out TOP will automatically repeat video frames to ensure the video and audio stay in sync. Recording a movie without frame drops can be done in non-realtime by turning off the Realtime flag at the top of the user interface. The length of the video is not predetermined and depends on the amount of time the Record parameter is on. You can record a sequence of .tif or .exr files by setting the Type parameter to Image Sequence. When Image File Type is set to OpenEXR, the EXR page has options to record any number of color channels from multiple TOPs into an EXR image file, and can create it with metadata that would get read by a Point File In TOP . The audio codecs that can be written out to file are ALAC (Apple Lossless), MP3, AAC, Vorbis, Opus, Uncompressed 16/32/64-bit (PCM). H264/H265/AV1 NOTE: Encoding movies in H.264/H.265/AV1 codec is only available with a Commercial or Pro license. NVIDIA graphic hardware is also required on Windows. On macoOS H264 is supported. Recording still images and stop-frame animation can be done by changing the 'Type' parameter. Then the 'Add Frame ' pulse button can be pulsed manually or via a script to cause the frames to be written. See also Movie File In TOP , Recording Movies with Audio , Video Stream Out TOP .

parameters.description: When saving out .dds file, mipmaps can be included if this is enabled. This is primarily used for the PreFilter Map TOP , which will encode special information into the mipmap levels of the texture which needs to be maintained.

parameters.name: resmult
parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. TOP.name: ncamTOP
TOP.description: NOTE License: Only available in TouchDesigner Pro . The Ncam TOP can receive image data from an external Ncam Reality tracking system for use in virtual production. To receive data, the TOP must reference an Ncam CHOP that is connected to the Ncam server. The type of image displayed in the TOP is chosen using the Output parameter. Multiple image streams may be available depending on the server settings, and additional Ncam TOPs can be used to access more than one stream. Possible image streams include the primary film stream captured by the external camera, a lens distortion map, and a depth image. The lens distortion map is a 32 bit floating point image where the R and G channels contain coordinates of where that pixel's color data should be taken from. The distortion map is used to warp a rendered image so that it matches the optical properties of an image captured with a physical lens. The lens distortion map can be applied to a rendered image by connecting a TOP with the rendered content to the Ncam TOP 's input and setting the Output parameter to 'Distort Input'. Additionally, the rendered content can be distorted and composited onto the film content using the 'Composite' option.

parameters.description: ⊞ - Select what type of output this TOP should produce. Some output modes like 'Composite' and 'Distort Input' require an input image from another TOP . Not all image streams may be available from the Ncam server. If a stream is not available, the TOP will produce an error.

parameters.description: Apply the lens distortion map to the input image and combine it on top of the film stream using the input image's alpha as a mask.

TOP.name: nDIInTOP
TOP.description: The NDI In TOP will obtain its image data over IP from other DI® (Network Data Interface) enabled applications. The NDI® protocol is created by Newtek . Attach an Audio NDI CHOP to the NDI In DAT to extract audio from the NDI stream. Metadata can also be sent to the NDI In TOP from an NDI Out TOP or another system that has attached metadata to the NDI stream. Attach an Info DAT to the NDI In DAT to get the metadata as text. It is in an XML format. To better see and access the XML, attach an XML DAT to the Info DAT . But you can also send a table-format DAT in the NDI Out TOP and it will be received in the Info DAT as a table. To send metadata in an NDI stream, see the NDI Out TOP 's Metadata DAT parameter. To see details of the available NDI streams, use the NDI DAT . See also NDI , NDI Out TOP and NDI DAT . NOTE for Windows OS - If experiencing connection issues, check Windows firewall settings.

The NDI Out TOP and other software based NDI solutions can only send native NDI, not NDI|HX. Currently only some hardware capture devices support streaming NDI|HX.

If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of the colors will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.description: Specify the frame rate to send at. Note that NDI uses the FPS partially as a guide to control how to compress the frames. The higher the FPS , the more compressed the frames will be. So for example sending at 1 FPS will result in higher image quality that sending at 30 FPS .

parameters.name: lowperformancebehavior
parameters.label: Low-Performance Behavior
parameters.description: ⊞ - When the NDI sending thread isn't able to keep up due to insufficient system resources (usually available CPU time), this controls the resulting behavior of the node.

parameters.name: stallmainthread
parameters.label: Stall Main Thread
parameters.description: The main thread will stall, giving up it's resources so the NDI sender can keep-up with the frames that are being sent. This will likely result in the main thread dropping frames.

parameters.name: skipframes
parameters.label: Skip Frames
parameters.description: The main thread will not stall, and instead will not give the sender new frames until it has processed the ones it currently has. This can result in the NDI sender being starved of CPU time and running at a far lower FPS than the main thread.

parameters.name: outputpixelformat
parameters.label: Output Pixel Format
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls the pixel format the output is encoded into.

parameters.name: fixed8
parameters.label: 8-bit

parameters.name: fixed16
parameters.label: 16-bit

parameters.name: includealpha

parameters.name: grouptable

parameters.name: audiochop

parameters.name: metadata

If the color space is unknown to the output form, then no metadata will be included.

If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of the colors will be adjusted to the range expected by the Output Color Space.
