TOP.name: substanceTOP
TOP.description: There is a tight integration between TouchDesigner and Adobe Substance 3D , a material creation package that is also node-based and has extensive material libraries. The Substance TOP allows you to load .sbsar files from Adobe Substance 3D to use with the PBR Material . The Substance TOP will load a material from a .sbsar file saved out from Substance Designer giving you access to all the parametric settings of the material inside TouchDesigner via automatically-generated parameters. Adjusting the parameters in TouchDesigner causes the materials to update on the fly. The Substance TOP outputs multiple images, one for each layer, typically five or more for base color, roughness, metallic, etc. The Substance TOP can be dragged to the PBR material which assigns all the layers to the appropriate PBR layers. Alternately, the Substance Select TOP can extract a single layer to which you can apply any TOP image operations, then assign the result to one of the PBR layer parameters.

parameters.name: file
parameters.label: Substance Designer File
parameters.description: Specify the .sbsar material file from Substance Designer.

parameters.name: reloadconfig
parameters.label: Reload File
parameters.description: Reloads the file from disk.

parameters.name: graph
parameters.label: Graph
parameters.description: Specify which graph in the .sbsar file to use. See Substance's Graph Help for more details.

parameters.name: output
parameters.label: Output
parameters.description: Choose what the output of the TOP will be. Grid Preview can be used to see all the texture maps inside the material at once.

parameters.name: invertnormal
parameters.label: Invert Normal Map
parameters.description: Inverts the normal map coming from the sbsar file. This parameter should be used when the normal map in the sbsar is -Y (DirectX) since normal map usage in TouchDesigner expects the normal map as Y+ (OpenGL).

parameters.name: engine
parameters.label: Engine
parameters.description: ⊞ - Select the Substance Engine used for rendering. The GPU engine has much lower render times and is the default engine, while the CPU is included as a legacy mode and was the engine used in TouchDesigner versions earlier than 2023.10000.

parameters.name: cpu
parameters.label: CPU
parameters.description: Render the textures using the Substance CPU Blend Engine. This is a legacy mode and was the engine used for TouchDesigner versions earlier than 2023.10000.

parameters.name: gpu
parameters.label: GPU
parameters.description: Render the textures using the Substance GPU Engine: Vulkan on Windows and Metal on macOS. The GPU engine will have quicker render times than the CPU engine.

parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the TOP the specified number of times. One exception to this is the GLSL TOP when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected TOP 's image.

TOP.name: subtractTOP
TOP.description: The Subtract TOP composites the input images together by subtracting the pixel values. Output = Input1 - Input2. The pixel values below 0 are clammped to 0. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.name: size
parameters.label: Fixed Layer
parameters.description: ⊞ - The selected input will become the fixed layer and the other input will be the overlay. This does not change the order of the composite (Input1 + Input2), only which layer is considered fixed and which layer is adjustable by the parameters on the Transform page. The resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer is used as the composite's final resolution and aspect ratio unless manually on the Common Page .

parameters.name: prefit
parameters.label: Pre-Fit Overlay
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how the Overlay layer (Overlay layer is the input that is NOT the Fixed Layer) fills the composite.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fill the resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: fithorz
parameters.label: Fit Horizontal
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer horizontally.

parameters.name: fitvert
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer vertically.

parameters.name: fitbest
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretch/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the best possible match that does not crop any of the Overlay layer. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: fitoutside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the worst possible match. This is the opposite of Best Fit. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Overlay is not squashed or stretched. The Overlay layer uses its own resolution and aspect ratio during the composite. Pixel accurate composites require Native Resolution , use this setting for to maintain an image's original resolution during the composite.

parameters.description: ⊞ - The menu attached to this parameter allows you to specify the order in which the changes to your TOP will take place. parameters.name: rord
parameters.label: Rotate Order
parameters.description: ⊞ - The rotational matrix presented when you click on this option allows you to set the transform order for the TOP 's rotations. As with transform order (above), changing the order in which the TOP 's rotations take place will alter the TOP 's final position.

parameters.name: p

parameters.name: resmult
parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this TOP is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.name: npasses
parameters.label: Passes
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the TOP the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the GLSL TOP when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected TOP 's image.

parameters.name: srgba8fixed
parameters.label: sRGB 8-bit fixed (RGBA)
parameters.description: Uses 8-bit integer values for each channel and stores color in sRGB colorspace. Note that this does not apply an sRGB curve to the pixel values, it only stores them using an sRGB curve. This means more data is used for the darker values and less for the brighter values. When the values are read downstream they will be converted back to linear. For more information refer to sRGB .

parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working Color Space before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: srgb
parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.description: Rec.601 with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec709
parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.description: Rec.709 color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020 color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.description: DCI-P3 color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim" color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.description: 1 - ACES 2065-1 (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acescg
parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.name: useparent
parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.description: Will use the Reference White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use Parent ' selected, then 'UI Reference White' will be used.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: ui
parameters.label: UI
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI Reference White Nits' value for it's brightness.

TOP.name: syphonSpoutInTOP
TOP.description: Note: For Spout on Windows, an Nvidia or AMD GPU is required, Intel does not work. The Syphon Spout In TOP will obtain its texture image via shared memory from other applications that support the Spout framework on Windows or Syphon on macOS. Since this uses shared memory, it only works on the computer it's running on and does not transmit textures across a network to another computer. To send textures to another computer, see Touch In TOP and Touch Out TOP , or NDI In TOP and NDI Out TOP . You can download a Spout setup package at http://spout.zeal.co/ for testing and example applications. You can download a Syphon simple server setup to testing. By default Spout on Windows is limited to 10 senders active on the computer. This limit can be changed by setting the Windows registry DWORD: HKEY_CURRENT_USER\\Software\\Leading Edge\\Spout\\MaxSenders See also: Syphon Spout Out TOP

TOP.name: textTOP
TOP.description: The Text TOP displays text strings in an image. It allows for multiple fonts, sizes, colors, borders, character separation and line separation. The text can be displayed as bit maps, anti-aliased lines, or filled polygon characters. Any TrueType font can be rendered by the Text TOP . Unicode is supported. The new Scalable Display Method uses Slug Library to render scalable, resolution independent text at the highest qulaity available in the Text TOP . It can display simple text strings with embedded numeric values. It can also format lines of text and numbers in decimal or floating point format, reading the numbers from a CHOP , using special formatting characters. It can also render text strings from a Table DAT via the Specification DAT parameter, where column headings are the parameter names that are to ve overidden when rendering a line of text for reach row of the table. Any TrueType or OpenType font that has been loaded into Windows can be rendered by the Text TOP . To import a new font into your Windows system, open the Fonts folder in the Control Panel , then drag and drop your font files in ( .ttf/.otf file format). Fonts can also be specified as .ttf/.otf file paths in the Font File parameter. You can render Unicode text by reading the text as a python string. See Unicode . Tip: You can use the textTOP_Class .textWidth member to calculate the width of the text in the Text TOP . See also: Field COMP , Text SOP , Unicode .

parameters.name: field
parameters.label: Field  Component
parameters.description: Specifies a Field Component to use as the source of the text. The font and style of the text displayed in the Field Component are set using the parameters in the Text TOP .

parameters.name: dat
parameters.label: DAT
parameters.description: Specifies a DAT to use for the source of the text. Drag and Drop a DAT onto this field, or manually enter the DAT 's path.

parameters.name: rowindex
parameters.label: DAT  Row
parameters.description: The row number (starting from 0) of the cell, if the DAT is a table.

parameters.name: colindex
parameters.label: DAT  Col
parameters.description: The column number of the cell, if the DAT is a table.

parameters.name: specdat
parameters.label: Specification  DAT
parameters.description: A Table DAT that allows you to specify and position text by pixel, with the lower left corner being at 0, 0. Column headers must include position1 or x , position2 or y , and text . A sample table can be:

parameters.name: text
parameters.label: Text
parameters.description: A string of text. It optionally can be followed by a numeric value and another post-string, as set with Value and Post Text below. If newlines or tabs are desired, the recommended way is to change this parameter to expression mode, and specify a Python string that includes \n or \t to signify newlines and tabs. E.g 'First Line\nSecond Line'.

parameters.name: legacyparsing
parameters.label: Legacy Parsing
parameters.description: In older builds the syntax \XXX (E.g \200 would be character 200), \t, \n as well as [] and {} (to position strings) was parsed in the string. This is now deprecated. For specifying characters codes, \t and \n Python syntax should be used instead. . The 'Specification DAT ' should be used to position strings instead of [], {}. This parameter can be enabled to turn back on this legacy parsing though. If this is enabled and you want to display the characters \ [ ] { } , you must precede them with a \ .

parameters.name: appendvalue
parameters.label: Append Value
parameters.description: Enables the Value field defined below. This value is inserted between the Text string and the Post Text string.

parameters.name: valuetouse
parameters.label: Value
parameters.description: The numeric value to display.

parameters.name: totaldigits
parameters.label: Total Digits
parameters.description: The total number of digits in the value displayed.

parameters.name: decimaldigits
parameters.label: Decimal Digits
parameters.description: The number of digits displayed after the decimal place.

parameters.name: posttext
parameters.label: Post Text
parameters.description: The text string appended after Text and Value (if present).

parameters.name: chopvaluereplace
parameters.label: CHOP  Value %-Replace
parameters.description: Allows portions of the strings to be replaced by CHOP values via a syntax similar to C-style printf()/sprintf(). More details of the syntax are provided in the next parameter, ' CHOP ' .

parameters.name: chop
parameters.label: CHOP
parameters.description: The CHOP containing all the values to insert in the Text strings. The Text TOP will repeat the Text string until all CHOP channels are displayed. They are displayed by using a special syntax in your Text string, defined as string starting with % , for example %4d :

parameters.label: flags  (optional)
parameters.description: Alignment options.

parameters.label: width  (optional)
parameters.description: Total number of digits in the number displayed.

parameters.label: precision  (optional)
parameters.description: Number of digits after the decimal place.

parameters.label: type
parameters.description: Number format.

parameters.name: wordwrap
parameters.label: Word Wrap
parameters.description: When checked text is automatically line wrapped so it doesn't extend outside the TOP 's borders. When using Word Wrap and Auto-Size together, the text will first word-wrap based on the specified font size, then auto size the resulting block of text.

parameters.name: smartquote
parameters.label: Smart Quote
parameters.description: Enables smart quotes which use a left (opening) quotation mark and a right (closing) quotation mark instead of straight quotes.

parameters.name: font
parameters.label: Font
parameters.description: Select the font for the text from this drop down menu. All fonts are provided by Windows, any TrueType font that is loaded into Windows can be used.

parameters.name: fontfile
parameters.label: Font File
parameters.description: Specify any TrueType font file ( .ttf file ) to use for the text. When using a font file, the Font menu above is disabled.

parameters.name: charset
parameters.label: Character Set
parameters.description: ⊞ - Select which character set to use.

parameters.name: dispmethod
parameters.label: Display Method
parameters.description: ⊞ - The display method used.

parameters.name: automatic
parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.description: Automatically chooses which display mode to use based on font size and settings.

parameters.name: polygon
parameters.label: Polygon
parameters.description: Uses polygons to display the text. Polygons look better using large font sizes. They also support anti-aliasing (see Anti-Aliased below).

parameters.name: stroke
parameters.label: Stroke
parameters.description: Same as polygons but only an outline of the text is displayed.

parameters.name: bitmap
parameters.label: Bitmap
parameters.description: Uses bitmap images for the text. Bitmap fonts are better for very small font sizes where high precision is required.

parameters.name: scalable
parameters.label: Scalable
parameters.description: Uses Slug Library to render high-quality, scalable, resolution independent text.

parameters.name: antialias
parameters.label: Anti-Alias
parameters.description: ⊞ - Smoothes out the edges of the text. Not available for Texture Display Mode.

parameters.name: strokewidth
parameters.label: Stroke Width
parameters.description: Controls the width of the outline when using Stroke Display Method.

parameters.name: bold
parameters.label: Bold
parameters.description: Displays the text in bold .

parameters.name: italic
parameters.label: Italic
parameters.description: Displays the text in Italic .

parameters.name: fontautosize
parameters.label: Auto-Size Font
parameters.description: ⊞ - Automatically controls font size using one of the following 3 options. When using this feature along with Word Wrap turned on, it will first word-wrap the text based on the specified font size, then auto size the resulting block of text.

parameters.name: nofit
parameters.label: No Auto-Fit
parameters.description: Does not use any auto-fitting. Font Size specified in Font Size X and Font Size Y parameters.

parameters.name: alwaysfit
parameters.label: Auto-Fit Always
parameters.description: The font size will be increased or decreased so the text fits across the Text TOP from edge to edge.

parameters.name: fitiffat
parameters.label: Auto-Fit if Too Large
parameters.description: Only auto sizes the text if the text is too large and spills past the edges of the Text TOP . In this case the font size will be decreased to fit it within the borders of the TOP .

parameters.name: fontsizex
parameters.label: Font Size X
parameters.description: Sets the font size in X (horizontal). Note: Floating point font sizes are permissable when using Polygon and Outline Display Methods .

parameters.name: fontsizexunit
parameters.label: Font Size X Unit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction, Fraction Aspect or Points (font point size). A Point is defined using the Windows conventions for 100% scaling, which is 96 pixels to 72 points. That is, a point size of 10 is the same as a pixel size of 10*(96/72) = 13.333.

parameters.name: fontsizey
parameters.label: Font Size Y
parameters.description: Sets the font size in Y (vertical). Note: Floating point font sizes are permissable when using Polygon and Outline Display Methods .

parameters.name: fontsizeyunit
parameters.label: Font Size Y Unit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction, Fraction Aspect or Points (font point size).

parameters.name: keepfontratio
parameters.label: Keep Font Ratio
parameters.description: Ignores Y value in Font Size. Sets both X and Y size to Font Size X.

parameters.name: breaklang
parameters.label: Break Language
parameters.description: Language type hint to help format the glyphs correctly.

parameters.name: readingdirection
parameters.label: Reading Direction
parameters.description: ⊞ - Use to set whether the language reads Left to Right or Right to Left.

parameters.name: tracking
parameters.label: Tracking
parameters.description: ⊞ - The amount of space to add between letters in X and Y. Tracking is way of adding an arbitrary offset between letters. There already is a default offset associated with each font so the letters are flush against each other. The Tracking parameter this adds to that and allows for a Y offset.

parameters.name: position
parameters.label: Position
parameters.description: ⊞ - The starting position of the text in X and Y.

parameters.label: [x,y]
parameters.description: "bleh[x,y]newtext" will place newtext at position (x,y) on the screen.

parameters.label: {X,Y}
parameters.description: "bleh{(+/-)x,(+/-)y}newtext" will offset newtext x,y from current position.

parameters.name: positionunit
parameters.label: Position Unit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.name: linespacing
parameters.label: Line Spacing
parameters.description: Determines the amount of space between lines of text.

parameters.name: linespacingunit
parameters.label: Line Spacing Unit
parameters.description: Select the units for this parameter from Pixels, Fraction (0-1), Fraction Aspect (0-1 considering aspect ratio).

parameters.description: Uses a bounding box around the text to position the text.

parameters.description: Top justifies the text.

parameters.description: ⊞ - Determines how vertical alignment is calculated.

parameters.name: metrics

parameters.description: Uses the font's built-in information to position the text.

parameters.name: bbox

parameters.description: Uses a bounding box around the text to position the text.

parameters.name: borderspace
parameters.label: Border Space

parameters.name: multrgbbyalpha
parameters.label: Multiply RGB by Alpha
parameters.description: Multiplies the RGB channels by the alpha channel.

parameters.description: ⊞ - RGBA values for the text displayed. (default: white (1,1,1,1))

parameters.description: What color the 2 top-most pixels are. Options are 0 (no change), Border A (uses color defined in Border A), or Border B (uses color defined in Border B).

parameters.name: topborderi

parameters.name: compoverinput
parameters.label: Comp Over Input
parameters.description: Turning this On will composite the input with the image.

parameters.name: operand
parameters.label: Operation
parameters.description: ⊞ - Choose which composite operation is performed from this menu. Search the web for 'blend modes' for more detailed information on the effects of each type.

parameters.name: add
parameters.label: Add
parameters.description: input1.rgba + input2.rgba

parameters.name: atop
parameters.label: Atop
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * input2.a) + (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a))

parameters.name: average
parameters.label: Average
parameters.description: (input1.rgba + input2.rgba)/2

parameters.name: difference
parameters.label: Difference
parameters.description: absoluteValue(input1.rgb - input2.rgb). Alpha always equals 1.0

parameters.name: divide
parameters.label: Divide
parameters.description: input1.rgba / input2.rgba

parameters.name: inside
parameters.label: Inside
parameters.description: input1.rgba * clamp(input2.a, 0.0, 1.0)

parameters.name: maximum
parameters.label: Maximum
parameters.description: max(input1.r, input2.r), max(input1.g, input2.g), max(input1.b, input2.b), max(input1.a, input2.a)

parameters.name: minimum
parameters.label: Minimum
parameters.description: min(input1.r, input2.r), min(input1.g, input2.g), min(input1.b, input2.b), min(input1.a, input2.a)

parameters.name: outside
parameters.label: Outside
parameters.description: input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)

parameters.name: over
parameters.label: Over
parameters.description: (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a)) + input1.rgba

parameters.name: screen
parameters.label: Screen
parameters.description: 1.0 - ((1.0 - input1.rgba) * (1.0 - input2.rgba))

parameters.name: subtract
parameters.label: Subtract
parameters.description: input1.rgba - input2.rgba

parameters.name: under
parameters.label: Under
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)) + input2.rgba

parameters.name: xor
parameters.label: Xor
parameters.description: (input1.rgba * (1.0 - input2.a)) + (input2.rgba * (1.0 - input1.a))

parameters.name: swaporder
parameters.label: Swap Order
parameters.description: Swaps the order of the composite with the input.

parameters.name: outputresolution
parameters.label: Output  Resolution
parameters.description: ⊞ - quickly change the resolution of the TOP 's data.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's resolution

parameters.name: eighth
parameters.label: Eighth
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: quarter
parameters.label: Quarter
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: half
parameters.label: Half
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 2x

parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 4x

parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: 8x
parameters.label: 8X
parameters.description: Multiply the input's resolution by that amount.

parameters.name: limit

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom  Resolution
parameters.description: Directly control the width and height.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: ⊞ - Enabled only when the Resolution parameter is set to Custom Resolution . Some Generators like Constant and Ramp do not use inputs and only use this field to determine their size. The drop down menu on the right provides some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.name: resmenu
parameters.label: Resolution  Menu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used resolutions.

parameters.name: resmult
parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.description: Uses the Global Resolution Multiplier found in Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this TOP is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.name: outputaspect
parameters.label: Output Aspect
parameters.description: ⊞ - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the input's aspect ratio.

parameters.name: resolution
parameters.label: Resolution
parameters.description: Uses the aspect of the image's defined resolution (ie 512x256 would be 2:1), whereby each pixel is square.

parameters.name: custom
parameters.label: Custom Aspect
parameters.description: Lets you explicitly define a custom aspect ratio in the Aspect parameter below.

parameters.name: aspect
parameters.label: Aspect
parameters.description: ⊞ - Use when Output Aspect parameter is set to Custom Aspect.

parameters.name: armenu
parameters.label: Aspect Menu
parameters.description: A drop-down menu with some commonly used aspect ratios.

parameters.name: inputfiltertype
parameters.label: Input Smoothness
parameters.description: ⊞ - This controls pixel filtering on the input image of the TOP .

parameters.name: nearest
parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: linear
parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. This is how you get TOP images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.description: Uses mipmap filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail.

parameters.name: fillmode
parameters.label: Fill  Viewer
parameters.description: ⊞ - Determine how the TOP image is displayed in the viewer.

parameters.name: useinput
parameters.label: Use Input
parameters.description: Uses the same Fill Viewer settings as it's input.

parameters.name: fill
parameters.label: Fill
parameters.description: Stretches the image to fit the edges of the viewer.

parameters.name: width

parameters.name: outside

parameters.name: filtertype

parameters.description: ⊞ - This controls pixel filtering in the viewers.

parameters.name: nearest
parameters.label: Nearest Pixel
parameters.description: Uses nearest pixel or accurate image representation. Images will look jaggy when viewing at any zoom level other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: linear
parameters.label: Interpolate Pixels
parameters.description: Uses linear filtering between pixels. Use this to get TOP images in viewers to look good at various zoom levels, especially useful when using any Fill Viewer setting other than Native Resolution .

parameters.name: mipmap
parameters.label: Mipmap Pixels
parameters.description: Uses mipmap filtering when scaling images. This can be used to reduce artifacts and sparkling in moving/scaling images that have lots of detail. When the input is 32-bit float format, only nearest filtering will be used (regardless of what is selected).

parameters.name: npasses
parameters.label: Passes
parameters.description: Duplicates the operation of the TOP the specified number of times. For every pass after the first it takes the result of the previous pass and replaces the node's first input with the result of the previous pass. One exception to this is the GLSL TOP when using compute shaders, where the input will continue to be the connected TOP 's image.

parameters.name: format

TOP.name: texture3DTOP
TOP.description: The Texture 3D TOP creates a 3D texture map. It saves a series of images in one array of pixels. This TOP can be used with Time Machine TOP , as well as materials. Using materials, a particular image in this array can be accessed by specifying a W texture coordinate, while the U and V coordinates are used to specify a texture location on that image. Refer to the 3D Texture article for more information. A 3D Texture can behave line a ring-buffer, or a FIFO (first-in, first-out) buffer, depending on it's usage scenario. For more information see the 3D Texture article. The Texture 3D TOP is similar to the Cache TOP which holds a set of images in a different form: the images are separate and you cannot use the W texture coordinate in a material to interpolate to access all of them in a shader. The Texture 3D TOP replaces one slice of its 3D data with its input every frame. When it has filled up all of its slices it wraps around and starts overwriting the oldest slice. The Texture 3D TOP can also create a 2D Texture Array . 2D Texture arrays are much like 3d textures, except are sampled using a non-normalized w texture coordinate. (i.e, 0 is the first slice, 1 is the 2nd slice, 2 is the 3rd slice etc.). Texture arrays also don't support blending between different slices when sampling at coordinate that falls between two slices. This a much faster alternative to 3d textures when interpolation between slices is not required. The non-normalized w coordinate makes it very easy to directly access a particular slice in the array. 2D Texture arrays also don't have a concept of w extend mode: they only work in their 0->(N-1) range. Locking the Texture 3D TOP preserves the entire 3D and 2D array in a .toe or .tox file. texture3dTOP_Class

parameters.name: texture3d

parameters.description: While this is set > 0, the Texture 3D TOP will replace the slice at 'Replace Index' with the input image. This allows you to replace specific slices of the 3D texture at will.

parameters.name: replacesinglepulse
parameters.label: Replace Single  Pulse
parameters.description: Replace an image for the single frame this was pulsed.

parameters.name: replaceindex
parameters.label: Replace Index
parameters.description: Select the slice index that will be replaced by the input, when 'Replace Single' is turned on.

parameters.name: prefill
parameters.label: Pre Fill
parameters.description: This feature is used to pre-setup all of the slices of the 3D texture in a single cook. When set to 1, it will fill the cache. If set to 1 during playback, it will fill immediately. If set to 1 and saved out, then next time the file is opened the cache will pre-fill. It sets up the cache by cooking its inputs at $F = 1, $F = 2, $F = 3 etc. up until the number of slice it needs to fill. Refer to Pre-Filling for more information.

parameters.name: prefillpulse
parameters.label: Pre Fill  Pulse
parameters.description: Pre-fills a single image during the frame this was pulsed.

parameters.name: cachesize
parameters.label: Cache Size
parameters.description: The number of images the Texture 3D TOP will hold. This is the number of 3D slices in the texture.

parameters.name: step
parameters.label: Step Size
parameters.description: This parameter sets how many frames pass before the TOP grabs one into cache. A Sample Step of 1 will grab each consecutive frame, a Sample Step of 2 will grab every other frame, and so on.

parameters.label: When Prefilling you would normally setup the inputs to the Texture 3D node in some way that is tied to $F. Such as a Movie File In  TOP  where set the Specify Index parameter to $F
parameters.description: 1 (since 0 is the first frame). Or a Noise TOP that is changing it's translation based on $F. If Step Size is 3, it would cook frame 1, 4, 7 etc.

parameters.name: reset
parameters.label: Reset
parameters.description: When set to 1, the cache is flushed and the TOP is reset.

parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.description: Instantly empty the cache.

TOP.name: timeMachineTOP
TOP.description: The Time Machine TOP combines pixels in a sequence of images stored in a Texture 3D TOP . Whereas "morphing" warps an image "spatially" (in xy), Time Machine warps images only in time. Time Machine, originally known as "tima" in PRISMS, was first used in 1995 for warping effects in Ghost in the Shell , a Japanese anime film that heavily used PRISMS for camera perspective effects, compositing, 3D and effects. You must connect a Texture 3D TOP to the Time Machine's first input. It uses this array of images and displays different depths of the 3D texture. The second input determines the time offset of the output image. The second input is expected to be monochrome, but uses the red channel when it is not monochrome. By default, where there is a black pixel in the second input, it gets the oldest layer of the 3D texture. Where there is a white pixel in the second input, it gets the most recent layer of the 3D texture. Black Offset and White Offset adjust the range of time that the black to white parts of the image are offset within. For example, if Black Offset is -10 and White Offset is 0, then a black pixel would be 10 frames behind in time, a white pixel the current frame, and a 50% grey pixel would be 5 frames behind in time (in between the Black and White Offsets).

parameters.description: Set the units for this parameter to index, frames, seconds or a fraction.

parameters.description: Sets the time offset for white areas of the Input 2 image.

TOP.name: toneMapTOP
TOP.description: Tone Mapping is the process of taking HDR content, that may have pixel brightness values much higher than 1, and re-ranging it down to the [0, 1] range, so it can be displayed on an SDR monitor. Without Tone Mapping, HDR content will look washed out on an SDR monitor, as all of the pixels that are >=1 will have the same brightness. So the sun will be the same brightness as a glossy highlight, for example. Tone Mapping does not aim to maintain the true brightness of the pixels when shown on the output display. That is what a true HDR display attempts to do. Instead is tries to re-range the values so different HDR brightness values still result in different SDR brightness values, even though initially they were both >= 1. This is entirely an artistic choice, so there is no 'right' Tone Mapping type to use. Each will give a different look, and the best one will depend on your content and what you prefer visually. An example project using this node can be found here : This node should not be used if you are outputting to an HDR display with HDR mode enabled.

parameters.description: A early Tone Map operation, described here . This one suffers from not using the full SDR range for the output in many cases. If the max values in a scene is (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), it will result in a final image being (0.5, 0.5, 0.5).

parameters.name: extendedreinhard

parameters.description: An improved version of the Reinhard tone map. Described here . This uses the Peak Input Nits to scale the input range better to the SDR output.

TOP.name: touchInTOP
TOP.description: The Touch In TOP will read in image data send over a TCP/IP network connection from a Touch Out TOP . The other TouchDesigner process can be on the same computer or from another computer anywhere on the connected network. It can receive Hap Q , Hap Q Alpha, and Uncompressed video. Make sure Windows Firewall settings are set to UNBLOCK for TouchDesigner, otherwise the data will be blocked. See also Touch Out TOP . For other protocols over IP see Video Stream Out TOP , Video Stream In TOP , NDI Out TOP and NDI In TOP . NOTE for Windows OS - If experiencing connection issues make sure Windows Firewall is disabled.

TOP.name: touchOutTOP
TOP.description: The Touch Out TOP sends a TOP image stream over TCP/IP to a Touch In TOP . The Touch In TOP can be in another TouchDesigner session on the same computer or on a computer anywhere on the connected network. It can output Hap Q , Hap Q Alpha, and Uncompressed video. Make sure Windows Firewall settings are set to UNBLOCK for TouchDesigner, otherwise the data will be blocked. See also Touch In TOP . For other protocols over IP see Video Stream Out TOP , Video Stream In TOP , NDI Out TOP and NDI In TOP . NOTE for Windows OS - If experiencing connection issues make sure Windows Firewall is disabled.

TOP.description: The Transform TOP applies 2D transformations to a TOP image like translate, scale, rotate, and multi-repeat tiling. The background can be filled with solid color and alpha.

parameters.description: ⊞ - The menu attached to this parameter allows you to specify the order in which the changes to your TOP will take place. parameters.label: Grow / Shrink

parameters.name: p
parameters.label: Pivot
parameters.description: ⊞ - The Pivot point edit fields allow you to define the point about which the TOP scales and rotates. Altering the pivot point of a TOP produces different results depending on the transformation performed on the TOP image.

parameters.label: For example, during a scaling operation, if the pivot point of a  TOP  image is located at
parameters.description: 1,-1 and you wanted to scale the image by 0.5 (reduce its size by 50%), then the TOP would scale toward the pivot point and appear to slide down and to the left.

parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working Color Space before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: srgb
parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.description: sRGB color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.description: Rec.601 with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: rec2020

parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.description: 1 - ACES 2065-1 (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acescg
parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.name: useparent
parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.description: Will use the Reference White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use Parent ' selected, then 'UI Reference White' will be used.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)

parameters.name: ui
parameters.label: UI

TOP.name: underTOP
TOP.description: The Under TOP places Input1 'under' Input2. The alpha of Input2 is used to determine what parts of the Input1 image are visible in the result. Note: This TOP supports 3D Textures and 2D Texture Arrays.

parameters.description: ⊞ - The selected input will become the fixed layer and the other input will be the overlay. This does not change the order of the composite (Input1 + Input2), only which layer is considered fixed and which layer is adjustable by the parameters on the Transform page. The resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer is used as the composite's final resolution and aspect ratio unless manually on the Common Page .

parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fill the resolution and aspect ratio of the Fixed Layer.

parameters.name: fitvert
parameters.label: Fit Vertical
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer vertically.

parameters.name: fitbest
parameters.label: Fit Best
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretch/squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the best possible match that does not crop any of the Overlay layer. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: fitoutside
parameters.label: Fit Outside
parameters.description: Overlay layer is stretched squashed to fit the Fixed Layer using the worst possible match. This is the opposite of Best Fit. The aspect ratio of the Overlay is maintained.

parameters.name: nativeres
parameters.label: Native  Resolution
parameters.description: Overlay is not squashed or stretched. The Overlay layer uses its own resolution and aspect ratio during the composite. Pixel accurate composites require Native Resolution , use this setting for to maintain an image's original resolution during the composite.

TOP.name: videoDeviceInTOP
TOP.description: The Video Device In TOP can be used to capture video from an external camera, capture card, capture dongle, IP camera, or video decoder connected to the system. Multiple devices can simultaneously stream video into TouchDesigner by using multiple Device In TOPs. HD-SDI video can be streamed into TouchDesigner through capture cards such and those from Blackmagic Design , AJA and Deltacast . If the device does not seem to provide a video stream but it is visible in the Cameras parameter menu, make sure no other applications are currently using the device. TIP : Create an Info DAT and point it to the Video Device In TOP to see what devices are currently attached. The Info CHOP gives data for analyzing the performance of Video Device In and Out TOPs. Additionally, the Info CHOP can be used to obtain timecode embeded into the source signal on some device, as indicated in the below list. Major capture devices vendors currently supported: Blackmagic Design - Supports Timecode. Windows and macOS. AJA - Supports Timecode. Windows only and macOS. Deltacast - Supports Timecode. Windows only. Bluefish444 - Supports Timecode. Windows only. Also supported with native drivers are some models from Datapath SDI, Allied Vision, Imaging Development Systems (IDS), FLIR/Point Grey, and Ximea. AJA and Blackmagic Design devices support 12-bit input and output formats, including AJA’s ability to capture at a full 12-bit RGB 4:4:4. For Magewell HDMI-to-USB3 capture (highly recommended, no drivers, plug-and-play), see Magewell . IP Cameras and USB3 include models from: Allied Vision - PvAPI SDK models only, not Vimba SDK. Prosilica Series and Manta cameras. Windows only. Point Grey FLIR Flycapture2 and Spinnaker - Windows only. Imaging Development Systems (IDS) - TouchDesigner implements both the uEye IDS Software Suite and the 'Peak' SDKs. GigE Vision cameras are currently not supported. Ximea - Windows only. Only a small subset of cameras from each manufacturer has been tested in-house, however it's expected that any modern camera from the supported manufacturer should work. If any issues are encountered please contact support@derivative.ca . See also Video Device Out TOP .

parameters.name: acescg

parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: acesproxy
parameters.label: ACESproxy
parameters.description: ACESproxy color space, which has a log transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough

parameters.name: inputreferencewhite
parameters.label: Input  Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting the input color values to the Working Color Space, this controls how they should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of the colors will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space detected/selected.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)

parameters.name: transfermode
parameters.label: Transfer Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls how the frames are transferred from the input device to CPU memory, and how they are transferred from CPU memory to the GPU .

parameters.name: automatic
parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.description: Will choose the best transfer mode for the components installed on the computer. In general this will be 'Pre-Upload'.

parameters.name: preupload
parameters.label: Pre-Upload
parameters.description: Upload the frames to the GPU as they arrived. This ensures the data is already in GPU memory when the GPU wants to process it.

parameters.name: ondemand
parameters.label: On-Demand
parameters.description: Only upload frames to the GPU if the TOP is going to display them for that cook. This reduces PCIe bandwidth between the GPU and CPU memory in cases where the TOP is showing less frames than what the input device is capturing. However this means the GPU may stall waiting for that frame to be uploaded.

parameters.name: ondemandsync
parameters.label: On-Demand, Sync to Frame Input
parameters.description: This mode is currently only available for AJA devices. This causes the whole TouchDesigner process to stall until right after a frame arrives on this input. Then the process will start executing and use that input frame for this nodes cook. This removes any latency from the capture input, but can result in worse performance. Real-time should turned off for the TouchDesigner process at the top of the UI, and only one node should be set to this mode in a single process.

parameters.name: memorymode
parameters.label: Memory Mode
parameters.description: ⊞ - Controls the memory type used to transfer data between the capture card and the GPU .

parameters.name: automatic
parameters.label: Automatic
parameters.description: Will choose the best memory mode for the transfer. This will be 'Pinned' for capture cards that support it, and 'Regular' if not.

parameters.name: pinned
parameters.label: Pinned
parameters.description: Pinned memory allows data to be transferred in 2 copies instead of three. Capture->Pinned CPU Memory, Pinned CPU Memory-> GPU Memory.

parameters.name: regular
parameters.label: Regular
parameters.description: The regular memory mode means 3 copies are required. Capture->Capture Writable Memory, Capture Writable Memory-> GPU Readable Memory, GPU Readable Memory-> GPU Memory.

parameters.name: syncinputs
parameters.label: Sync Inputs
parameters.description: Enabling syncing of multiple Video Device In TOPs. Syncing allows multiple nodes using multiple inputs and capture cards on a single system to ensure they are outputting frames in sync. Without this each node will be free running and will possible be outputting frames that came it at different times due to internal queuing. It's important the input sources are GenLocked to ensure all of their data arrives to all of the inputs at the same time, otherwise syncing will not work. This feature is currently supported for Blackmagic, DataPath, Deltacast and BlueFish devices.

parameters.name: syncgroupindex
parameters.label: Sync  Group  Index
parameters.description: There can be multiple sync groups active in a .toe file. Nodes will only sync to other nodes that are part of the same sync group.

parameters.name: maxsyncoffset
parameters.label: Max Sync Offset (ms)
parameters.description: Specified in milliseconds. The maximum difference in time two image could have arrived at be considered in-sync. Images that arrive at times more different than this offset will be considered to be part of different 'frame'.

parameters.name: synctimeout
parameters.label: Sync Timeout (ms)
parameters.description: How much time to wait for all frames in a sync group to become available before giving up trying to sync. Expressed in milliseconds. If this timeout elapses when waiting for a frame from one or more sources in the sync group, all of the nodes in the sync group will keep their current image and not output a new image, even if some new images arrived on some of the inputs.

If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global Resolution Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. parameters.name: dcip3d60

parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim" color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: displayp3d65

parameters.description: Display-P3 color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: aces2065

parameters.name: acescg
parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.description: ACEScg (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to Reference White.

parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.description: ⊞ - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same Reference White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the Reference White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR Reference White of 120 nits, and the HDR Reference White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.name: default
parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR Reference White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.name: useparent
parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.description: Will use the Reference White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use Parent ' selected, then 'UI Reference White' will be used.

parameters.name: sdr
parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: hdr
parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.name: ui
parameters.label: UI
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI Reference White Nits' value for it's brightness.

parameters.label: connected
parameters.description: 1 if the node is successfully connected to the device, 0 if not. This does not necessarily mean there is valid input coming to the device.

parameters.label: sync_timeouts
parameters.description: When using the 'Sync Group ' feature, this counts how many times the group failed to all provide a frame with similar enough timestamps within the timeout period.

parameters.label: last_sync_wait
parameters.description: How long the node had to wait from the time it was ready for a new frame until all the inputs provided valid frames for a synced output.

parameters.label: odd_field
parameters.description: When de-interlacing an interlaced input, this will be 1 when the odd field is being shown and 0 when the even field is being shown.

parameters.label: capture_fps
parameters.description: The calculated number of frames per second that are being captured by the device. This does not map directly to the signal format rate. It won't show 59.97 for example. This is simply a count of how many frames were captured in the last 1000ms.

parameters.label: capture_total
parameters.description: The total number of frames that have been captured this capture began.

parameters.label: frames_repeated
parameters.description: How many times the node has shown the same frame more than once. It does not currently correct for if the repeats are expected, such as when capturing a 30hz signal but TouchDesigner is running at 60fps. In that case the channel will keep increasing since each captured frame will be shown twice.

parameters.label: frames_dropped
parameters.description: This counts how many frames were captured by the card, but never consumed by TouchDesigner's reading thread. This occurs if the capture is running faster than TouchDesigner is able to consume frames.

parameters.label: frames_skipped
parameters.description: This counts how many frames were consumed by TouchDesigner's reading thread, but never consumed by the node itself. This can occur if TouchDesigner isn't running at full frame rate.

parameters.label: connection_changes
parameters.description: Counts connection changes, not supported by all devices.

parameters.label: temperature
parameters.description: On supported devices, outputs the temperature of the device in celsius. Will be a very negative number for devices that don't support it.

parameters.label: signal_fps
parameters.description: The actual signal format FPS of the input signal. 0 if unknown.

parameters.label: rgb_input
parameters.description: Will be 1 if the input is detected as an RGB (such as RGB 4:4:4) format. 0 if it is a YUV/YCbCr based. -1 if it is unknown or not supported by the the library.

parameters.label: frame_queue_length
parameters.description: The number of receieved frames queued inside TouchDesigner.

parameters.label: frame_hw_queue_length
parameters.description: The number of frames still queued on the device that TouchDesigner has not yet read.

parameters.label: last_dma_copy_time
parameters.description: The number of milliseconds it took to copy the last frame from the device to the CPU. -1 if this is not measured.

parameters.label: frame_timestamp
parameters.description: Time in seconds of the last frame displayed. -1 if this is not provided by the device.

parameters.label: resx
parameters.description: Horizontal resolution of the TOP in pixels.

parameters.label: resy
parameters.description: Vertical resolution of the TOP in pixels.

parameters.label: aspectx
parameters.description: Horizontal aspect of the TOP .

parameters.label: aspecty
parameters.description: Vertical aspect of the TOP .

parameters.label: depth
parameters.description: Depth of 2D or 3D array if this TOP contains a 2D or 3D texture array.

parameters.label: gpu_memory_used
parameters.description: Total amount of texture memory used by this TOP .

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.
